qe: While alkali and alkaline earth metals generally impart distinct flame colors due to low ionization energies and thermal electron excitation, two specific Group-2 metals fail to show any characteristic flame coloration. Which pair of metals exhibits this exception, and why?
qh: जबकि क्षार और क्षारीय मृदा धातुएं कम आयनन ऊर्जा और तापीय इलेक्ट्रॉन उत्तेजन के कारण आम तौर पर विशिष्ट ज्वाला रंग प्रदान करती हैं, दो विशिष्ट समूह-2 धातुएं कोई विशिष्ट ज्वाला रंग दिखाने में विफल रहती हैं। कौन सी धातु जोड़ी इस अपवाद को प्रदर्शित करती है, और क्यों?
o: Lithium and Sodium, because their outer electrons are shielded by d-subshells.
Beryllium and Magnesium, because of their small atomic sizes and high ionization energies.
Calcium and Strontium, because their high atomic masses absorb visible light frequencies.
Barium and Radium, because they undergo immediate alpha decay upon heating.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies alkali metals that show golden yellow and crimson/violet flames. Option 1 is correct because Beryllium ($\\text{Be}$) and Magnesium ($\\text{Mg}$) have small atomic radii and exceptionally high **Ionization Energy** [the minimum thermodynamic energy required to remove the most loosely bound electron from an isolated neutral gaseous atom]. The thermal energy produced by a Bunsen burner flame is insufficient to excite their tightly bound valence electrons to higher electronic energy levels. Consequently, no visible photons are emitted when returning to the ground state. Option 2 lists calcium (brick red) and strontium (crimson red), which do impart flame color. Option 3 introduces radioactive decay as a false distractor.

qe: A laboratory analyst conducts flame test verification for a group of s-block elements. Which option correctly pairs the s-block metal with its corresponding flame emission color?
qh: एक प्रयोगशाला विश्लेषक s-ब्लॉक तत्वों के समूह के लिए ज्वाला परीक्षण सत्यापन करता है। कौन सा विकल्प s-ब्लॉक धातु को उसके संबंधित ज्वाला उत्सर्जन रंग के साथ सही ढंग से मिलाता है?
o: Sodium: Brick Red; Potassium: Apple Green; Barium: Crimson
Sodium: Golden Yellow; Calcium: Crimson Red; Barium: Apple Green
Lithium: Golden Yellow; Strontium: Violet; Potassium: Apple Green
Calcium: Golden Yellow; Barium: Crimson Red; Sodium: Apple Green
e: Explanation: Option 0 misassigns colors across sodium, potassium, and barium. Option 1 is correct because when s-block metal valence electrons are thermally excited in a flame, they emit light at specific visible wavelengths upon relaxation: **Sodium ($\\text{Na}$)** emits **Golden Yellow**, **Calcium ($\\text{Ca}$)** emits **Crimson Red / Brick Red**, and **Barium ($\\text{Ba}$)** emits **Apple Green**. Option 2 incorrectly pairs lithium with yellow (lithium gives violet/crimson) and potassium with green. Option 3 completely scrambles all metallic flame pairings.

qe: Pure table salt ($\\text{NaCl}$) is non-hygroscopic. However, commercial common salt samples often absorb moisture from humid air and turn soggy. What impurity drives this hygroscopic transformation?
qh: शुद्ध टेबल नमक ($\\text{NaCl}$) गैर-आर्द्रताग्राही होता है। हालाँकि, वाणिज्यिक साधारण नमक के नमूने अक्सर आर्द्र हवा से नमी अवशोषित करते हैं और गीले हो जाते हैं। कौन सी अशुद्धि इस आर्द्रताग्राही परिवर्तन को संचालित करती है?
o: Traces of elemental sodium and volatile ammonia gas.
Impurities of Magnesium Chloride ($\\text{MgCl}_2$) and Calcium Chloride ($\\text{CaCl}_2$).
High concentrations of Chile Saltpetre ($\\text{NaNO}_3$).
Insoluble Borax ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{B}_4\\text{O}_7 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) crystals.
e: Explanation: Option 0 is incorrect because elemental sodium reacts violently with water rather than absorbing air moisture passively. Option 1 is correct because pure **Sodium Chloride ($\\text{NaCl}$)** is not **Hygroscopic** [the chemical property of a substance to spontaneously absorb and retain water molecules from the surrounding atmospheric environment]. Commercial sea salt contains trace impurities of **Magnesium Chloride ($\\text{MgCl}_2$) and Calcium Chloride ($\\text{CaCl}_2$)**, both of which are deliquescent salts that readily absorb moisture, making the salt clump. Option 2 and Option 3 list non-deliquescent sodium ores.

qe: Industrial extraction of metallic sodium relies on specific electrolytic operations to avoid side reactions. Which extraction method matches the raw material used for obtaining pure sodium?
qh: धात्विक सोडियम का औद्योगिक निष्कर्षण पार्श्व प्रतिक्रियाओं से बचने के लिए विशिष्ट इलेक्ट्रोलाइटिक संचालन पर निर्भर करता है। शुद्ध सोडियम प्राप्त करने के लिए उपयोग किए जाने वाले कच्चे माल से कौन सी निष्कर्षण विधि मेल खाती है?
o: Electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride in the Solvay process.
Electrolysis of molten $\\text{NaOH}$ in Castner's process or molten $\\text{NaCl}$ in Down's process.
Carbon thermal reduction of Glauber's salt in a blast furnace.
Leaching of Chile saltpetre with concentrated nitric acid.
e: Explanation: Option 0 is incorrect because electrolyzing aqueous $\\text{NaCl}$ yields hydrogen gas at the cathode instead of metallic sodium. Option 1 is correct because sodium is an electropositive metal with high reduction potential, meaning it cannot be reduced using carbon. It is extracted by **Electrolytic Reduction** of fused (molten) salts: **Castner's Process** electrolyzes molten **Sodium Hydroxide ($\\text{NaOH}$)**, while **Down's Process** electrolyzes molten **Sodium Chloride ($\\text{NaCl}$)** mixed with $\\text{CaCl}_2$ to lower the melting point. Option 2 and Option 3 describe pyrometallurgical methods that fail for alkali metals.

qe: An organic synthesis laboratory uses metallic sodium as a reducing agent. When sodium metal is treated with pure liquid ammonia and anhydrous ethyl alcohol respectively, what chemical products are synthesized?
qh: एक कार्बनिक संश्लेषण प्रयोगशाला अपचायक एजेंट के रूप में धात्विक सोडियम का उपयोग करती है। जब सोडियम धातु को क्रमशः शुद्ध तरल अमोनिया और निर्जल एथिल अल्कोहल के साथ उपचारित किया जाता है, तो कौन से रासायनिक उत्पाद संश्लेषित होते हैं?
o: Sodium hydride with ammonia; Sodium nitrate with alcohol.
Sodamide ($\\text{NaNH}_2$) with ammonia; Sodium alkoxide ($\\text{C}_2\\text{H}_5\\text{ONa}$) and $\\text{H}_2$ gas with alcohol.
Sodium peroxide with ammonia; Pure carbon monoxide with alcohol.
Sodium carbonate with ammonia; Benzene rings with alcohol.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes incorrect salt products. Option 1 is correct because metallic sodium reacts with dry ammonia gas or liquid ammonia in the presence of a catalyst to yield **Sodamide ($\\text{NaNH}_2$)** and hydrogen gas. When treated with anhydrous ethyl alcohol ($\\text{C}_2\\text{H}_5\\text{OH}$), sodium displaces the weakly acidic hydroxylic proton, forming **Sodium Alkoxide / Ethoxide ($\\text{C}_2\\text{H}_5\\text{ONa}$)** and liberating **Hydrogen Gas ($\\text{H}_2$)**. Option 2 and Option 3 present incorrect oxidation or ring-synthesis pathways.

qe: Liquid sodium metal is used in specialized engineering applications, such as modern nuclear power stations. What physical property makes liquid sodium suitable for this specific application?
qh: द्रव सोडियम धातु का उपयोग विशिष्ट इंजीनियरिंग अनुप्रयोगों में किया जाता है, जैसे कि आधुनिक परमाणु ऊर्जा स्टेशन। कौन सा भौतिक गुण द्रव सोडियम को इस विशिष्ट अनुप्रयोग के लिए उपयुक्त बनाता है?
o: It acts as a neutron moderator that absorbs gamma radiation.
It has high thermal conductivity and a wide liquid temperature range, serving as an efficient coolant in fast breeder nuclear reactors.
It completely converts radioactive waste into solid Glauber's salt.
It acts as an insoluble organic solvent that dissolves heavy lead plates.
e: Explanation: Option 0 confuses thermal coolants with neutron moderators (like heavy water or graphite). Option 1 is correct because liquefied sodium exhibits high thermal conductivity, low viscosity, and a wide liquid range (melting at $\\sim 98^\\circ\\text{C}$ and boiling at $\\sim 883^\\circ\\text{C}$). This enables it to transfer thermal energy away from the reactor core without requiring high pressure systems, making it an efficient **Liquid Metal Coolant** in nuclear reactors. Option 2 and Option 3 introduce incorrect waste-disposal or heavy-lead solvation claims.

qe: Although most metals react with dilute mineral acids to liberate hydrogen gas, nitric acid ($\\text{HNO}_3$) generally prevents hydrogen evolution. Which two metals defy this rule by evolving hydrogen gas when treated with very dilute $\\text{HNO}_3$?
qh: यद्यपि अधिकांश धातुएँ तनु खनिज अम्लों के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करके हाइड्रोजन गैस मुक्त करती हैं, नाइट्रिक अम्ल ($\\text{HNO}_3$) सामान्यतः हाइड्रोजन के निकलने को रोकता है। कौन सी दो धातुएं बहुत तनु $\\text{HNO}_3$ के साथ उपचारित होने पर हाइड्रोजन गैस निकालकर इस नियम का उल्लंघन करती हैं?
o: Copper ($\\text{Cu}$) and Silver ($\\text{Ag}$)
Magnesium ($\\text{Mg}$) and Manganese ($\\text{Mn}$)
Sodium ($\\text{Na}$) and Potassium ($\\text{K}$)
Gold ($\\text{Au}$) and Platinum ($\\text{Pt}$)
e: Explanation: Option 0 features unreactive metals that require concentrated $\\text{HNO}_3$ to yield nitrogen oxides without $\\text{H}_2$. Option 1 is correct because nitric acid is a strong **Oxidizing Agent** [a chemical species that oxidizes other substances while being reduced itself], converting liberated $\\text{H}_2$ into $\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$ and forming nitrogen oxides ($\\text{N}_2\\text{O}, \\text{NO}, \\text{NO}_2$). However, **Magnesium ($\\text{Mg}$) and Manganese ($\\text{Mn}$)** have high oxidation potentials. When treated with *very dilute* ($\\sim 1-2\\%$) $\\text{HNO}_3$, the oxidizing power of the acid is minimized, allowing these two metals to reduce protons and evolve **Hydrogen Gas ($\\text{H}_2$)**. Option 2 describes metals that react violently with water content, and Option 3 lists noble metals.

qe: In medical biochemistry, maintaining the precise physiological concentration of sodium ions ($\\text{Na}^+$) is crucial for human health. What is the daily sodium requirement for an adult, and what primary biological functions depend on it?
qh: चिकित्सा जैव रसायन में, सोडियम आयनों ($\\text{Na}^+$) की सटीक शारीरिक सांद्रता को बनाए रखना मानव स्वास्थ्य के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है। एक वयस्क के लिए दैनिक सोडियम की आवश्यकता क्या है, और कौन से प्राथमिक जैविक कार्य इस पर निर्भर करते हैं?
o: 50 mg per day; regulates bone density and hemoglobin synthesis.
500 mg per day; regulates blood pressure, osmotic balance, and body pH.
5000 mg per day; acts as a structural component of tooth hydroxyapatite.
5 mg per day; drives the enzymatic degradation of stomach pepsin.
e: Explanation: Option 0 severely underestimates the required mass and assigns calcium/iron functions to sodium. Option 1 is correct because the human body requires approximately **$500\\text{ mg}$ of Sodium per day**. As the chief extracellular cation, $\\text{Na}^+$ controls **Osmotic Pressure** [the hydrostatic pressure required to prevent the inward flow of water across a semipermeable membrane], regulates blood pressure, maintains fluid volume, and stabilizes body pH. Rapid salt loss during severe dehydration or vomiting disrupts this osmotic balance. Option 2 overstates the daily baseline tenfold and lists calcium enamel functions. Option 3 presents an incorrect enzyme function.

qe: Aluminium oxide ($\\text{Al}_2\\text{O}_3$) and Zinc oxide ($\\text{ZnO}$) show dual chemical reactivity by forming salts with both strong acids and strong bases. What term defines this dual behavior, and what product forms when $\\text{ZnO}$ reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
qh: एल्यूमीनियम ऑक्साइड ($\\text{Al}_2\\text{O}_3$) और जिंक ऑक्साइड ($\\text{ZnO}$) प्रबल अम्लों और प्रबल क्षारों दोनों के साथ लवण बनाकर दोहरी रासायनिक प्रतिक्रियाशीलता दिखाते हैं। कौन सा शब्द इस दोहरे व्यवहार को परिभाषित करता है, और जब $\\text{ZnO}$ जलीय सोडियम हाइड्रोक्साइड के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करता है तो कौन सा उत्पाद बनता है?
o: Basic oxides; yields Zinc hydroxide and hydrogen gas.
Amphoteric oxides; yields Sodium zincate ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{ZnO}_2$) and water.
Neutral oxides; yields Zinc chloride and ozone gas.
Deliquescent oxides; yields Sodium peroxide and zinc powder.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misclassifies the oxide as purely basic. Option 1 is correct because metal oxides that react with both acids and bases to produce a salt and water are called **Amphoteric Oxides** [oxides that can act as either an acid or a base depending on the reaction partner]. When $\\text{ZnO}$ reacts with a strong base like $\\text{NaOH}$, it behaves as an acidic oxide: $\\text{ZnO} + 2\\text{NaOH} \\rightarrow \\text{Na}_2\\text{ZnO}_2 + \\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. The product is **Sodium Zincate ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{ZnO}_2$)**. Option 2 and Option 3 describe neutral or deliquescent pathways that do not apply to zinc oxide.

qe: Evaluating the activity of metals with water shows distinct temperature thresholds. Which metal requires steam to form a metal oxide and hydrogen, rather than reacting with cold or hot liquid water?
qh: पानी के साथ धातुओं की गतिविधि का मूल्यांकन अलग-अलग तापमान सीमाओं को दर्शाता है। किस धातु को ठंडे या गर्म तरल पानी के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करने के बजाय धातु ऑक्साइड और हाइड्रोजन बनाने के लिए भाप (steam) की आवश्यकता होती है?
o: Potassium ($\\text{K}$)
Sodium ($\\text{Na}$)
Aluminium ($\\text{Al}$)
Calcium ($\\text{Ca}$)
e: Explanation: Option 0, 1, and 3 list highly reactive metals (K, Na, Ca) that react vigorously with cold liquid water to form hydroxides ($\\text{KOH}, \\text{NaOH}, \\text{Ca(OH)}_2$) and hydrogen gas. Option 2 is correct because moderately reactive metals like **Aluminium ($\\text{Al}$), Iron ($\\text{Fe}$), and Zinc ($\\text{Zn}$)** do not react with cold or hot liquid water. They require high-temperature **Steam ($\\text{H}_2\\text{O}_{(g)}$)** to drive oxidation, producing the metal oxide and hydrogen gas: $2\\text{Al} + 3\\text{H}_2\\text{O}_{(g)} \\rightarrow \\text{Al}_2\\text{O}_3 + 3\\text{H}_2$. Least reactive metals like $\\text{Pb}, \\text{Cu}, \\text{Ag}, \\text{Au}$ do not react with water or steam at all.

qe: According to the Reactivity Series of metals, a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its aqueous salt solution. Which single displacement reaction will occur spontaneously?
qh: धातुओं की प्रतिक्रियाशीलता श्रेणी (Reactivity Series) के अनुसार, एक अधिक प्रतिक्रियाशील धातु अपने जलीय लवण घोल से कम प्रतिक्रियाशील धातु को विस्थापित कर देती है। कौन सी एकल विस्थापन प्रतिक्रिया स्वतःस्फूर्त (spontaneously) होगी?
o: $\\text{Cu} + \\text{FeSO}_4(aq) \\rightarrow \\text{CuSO}_4(aq) + \\text{Fe}$
$\\text{Fe} + \\text{CuSO}_4(aq) \\rightarrow \\text{FeSO}_4(aq) + \\text{Cu}\\downarrow$
$\\text{Ag} + \\text{ZnSO}_4(aq) \\rightarrow \\text{Ag}_2\\text{SO}_4(aq) + \\text{Zn}$
$\\text{Au} + \\text{HCl}(aq) \\rightarrow \\text{AuCl}_3(aq) + \\text{H}_2$
e: Explanation: Option 0 is non-spontaneous because Copper is positioned below Iron in the activity series ($\\text{Fe} > \\text{Cu}$). Option 1 is correct because Iron ($\\text{Fe}$) sits higher in the **Reactivity Series** [an arrangement of metallic elements in decreasing order of their standard electrode oxidation potentials] than Copper ($\\text{Cu}$). Therefore, Iron easily donates electrons to reduce $\\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ions, displacing brown metallic copper from a blue copper sulphate solution: $\\text{Fe} + \\text{CuSO}_4 \\rightarrow \\text{FeSO}_4 + \\text{Cu}\\downarrow$. Option 2 and Option 3 feature unreactive noble metals (Ag, Au) trying to displace highly reactive metals (Zn, H), which is thermodynamically impossible under standard conditions.

qe: Evaluating the physical properties of alkali metals shows that Lithium exhibits notable differences from Sodium and Potassium. Which statement correctly identifies a unique property of Lithium?
qh: क्षार धातुओं के भौतिक गुणों का मूल्यांकन दर्शाता है कि लिथियम सोडियम और पोटेशियम से उल्लेखनीय अंतर प्रदर्शित करता है। कौन सा कथन लिथियम के एक अद्वितीय गुण की सही पहचान करता है?
o: It is the heaviest known transition element and a weak oxidizing agent.
It is the lightest metallic element and acts as a very strong reducing agent.
It exists as a liquid at room temperature and is stored in water.
It reacts with cold water without liberating any gas.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misclassifies lithium as a heavy transition metal. Option 1 is correct because **Lithium ($\\text{Li}$)** is the **Lightest Metallic Element** (density $\\rho \\approx 0.534\\text{ g/cm}^3$, floating even on kerosene oil). Despite its small atomic size, its exceptionally high hydration enthalpy gives it the most negative standard reduction potential ($E^\\circ = -3.04\\text{ V}$) among all elements, making it a very strong **Reducing Agent** in aqueous solution. Option 2 and Option 3 confuse lithium with liquid mercury or propose an impossible gasless water reaction.

qe: At room temperature, metals like magnesium, aluminium, zinc, and lead do not undergo continuous atmospheric oxidation. What structural barrier prevents these metals from corroding further?
qh: कमरे के तापमान पर, मैग्नीशियम, एल्यूमीनियम, जस्ता और सीसा जैसी धातुएँ निरंतर वायुमंडलीय ऑक्सीकरण से नहीं गुज़रती हैं। कौन सी संरचनात्मक बाधा इन धातुओं को और अधिक संक्षारित होने से रोकती है?
o: A continuous layer of liquid mercury amalgam on their surfaces.
A thin, protective, self-passivating layer of oxide that seals the underlying metal from oxygen.
A waxy organic suberin coating synthesized by ambient light.
An insoluble surface coating of pure sodium nitrate.
e: Explanation: Option 0 introduces mercury amalgams, which accelerate oxidation rather than preventing it. Option 1 is correct because metals such as $\\text{Mg}, \\text{Al}, \\text{Zn}, \\text{Pb}$ undergo spontaneous surface oxidation upon air exposure, forming a thin, impermeable, tightly adherent **Protective Oxide Layer** ($\\text{MgO}, \\text{Al}_2\\text{O}_3, \\text{ZnO}, \\text{PbO}$). This **Passivation** layer acts as a physical barrier that prevents further oxygen diffusion to the underlying metal atoms. Option 2 and Option 3 list plant anatomical compounds or soluble sodium salts.

qe: The physical form of a metal significantly affects its combustion kinetics. How does a solid iron bar behave in a burner flame compared to finely divided iron filings?
qh: धातु का भौतिक रूप इसके दहन गतिकी (combustion kinetics) को महत्वपूर्ण रूप से प्रभावित करता है। बर्नर की लौ में लोहे का चूरा (iron filings) लोहे की एक ठोस छड़ की तुलना में कैसा व्यवहार करता है?
o: The solid iron bar burns with a bright yellow flame, whereas iron filings do not react.
The solid iron bar does not burn on heating, but iron filings burn vigorously when sprinkled into the burner flame due to increased surface area.
Both forms evaporate into nitrogen dioxide gas within seconds.
Iron filings dissolve into an aqueous basic solution without releasing heat.
e: Explanation: Option 0 reverses the combustion kinetics between bulk and powdered metal. Option 1 is correct because combustion depends on **Surface Area to Volume Ratio**. A bulk solid iron bar has a low surface area exposed to atmospheric oxygen; when heated, it glows red and forms a surface oxide layer without burning. In contrast, **Finely Divided Iron Filings** have a large surface area, allowing rapid oxygen contact and thermal absorption. When sprinkled into a flame, they oxidize rapidly and burn vigorously. Option 2 and Option 3 describe impossible phase changes or wet dissolution paths.

qe: Sodium is an alkali metal located in Group-1 and Period-3 of the Modern Periodic Table. What is its valence electronic configuration, and what percentage of the Earth's crust does it comprise by weight?
qh: सोडियम आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी के समूह-1 और आवर्त-3 में स्थित एक क्षार धातु है। इसका संयोजी इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास क्या है, और यह भार के अनुसार पृथ्वी की पपड़ी का कितना प्रतिशत हिस्सा है?
o: Configuration: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2$; Crust abundance: 12.5%
Configuration: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^1$; Crust abundance: 2.27% by weight
Configuration: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^5$; Crust abundance: 0.01%
Configuration: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^1$; Crust abundance: 50.0%
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists magnesium's $3s^2$ electronic configuration and overstates abundance. Option 1 is correct because Sodium ($\\text{Na}$, $Z=11$, atomic mass $\\approx 23\\text{ u}$) has the ground-state **Electronic Configuration** $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^1$ (or $[\\text{Ne}]3s^1$). Due to its high chemical reactivity, it never occurs in a free elemental state in nature. It constitutes **2.27% of the Earth's Crust by weight**, making it one of the most abundant alkali metals in combined mineral forms. Option 2 lists fluorine's configuration, and Option 3 lists aluminium's configuration.

qe: Sodium forms several natural mineral deposits in the Earth's crust. Which choice correctly matches the mineral name with its corresponding chemical formula?
qh: सोडियम पृथ्वी की पपड़ी में कई प्राकृतिक खनिज जमा बनाता है। कौन सा विकल्प खनिज के नाम को उसके संबंधित रासायनिक सूत्र के साथ सही ढंग से मिलाता है?
o: Chile Saltpetre: $\\text{Na}_2\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$; Glauber's Salt: $\\text{NaNO}_3$
Chile Saltpetre: $\\text{NaNO}_3$; Glauber's Salt: $\\text{Na}_2\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$; Borax: $\\text{Na}_2\\text{B}_4\\text{O}_7 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$
Chile Saltpetre: $\\text{NaCl}$; Glauber's Salt: $\\text{NaOH}$
Borax: $\\text{NaNO}_3$; Glauber's Salt: $\\text{Na}_2\\text{CO}_3 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$
e: Explanation: Option 0 swaps the chemical formulas of Chile Saltpetre and Glauber's salt. Option 1 is correct because the principal natural mineral ores of sodium include: **Chile Saltpetre** (Sodium Nitrate, $\\text{NaNO}_3$), **Glauber's Salt** (Hydrated Sodium Sulphate, $\\text{Na}_2\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$), **Borax** (Hydrated Sodium Tetraborate, $\\text{Na}_2\\text{B}_4\\text{O}_7 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$), and **Brine / Common Salt** ($\\text{NaCl}$). Option 2 misidentifies table salt as Chile Saltpetre, and Option 3 confuses Borax with nitrate ores.

qe: Sodium metal is stored immersed in kerosene oil. Why is kerosene used, and in which organic solvent is sodium metal soluble without undergoing a violent reaction?
qh: सोडियम धातु को मिट्टी के तेल (kerosene oil) में डुबो कर रखा जाता है। मिट्टी के तेल का उपयोग क्यों किया जाता है, और किस कार्बनिक विलायक (organic solvent) में सोडियम धातु बिना हिंसक प्रतिक्रिया के घुलनशील है?
o: Stored in kerosene to prevent reaction with atmospheric oxygen/water; soluble in Benzene.
Stored in kerosene to increase its density; soluble in concentrated mineral acids.
Stored in kerosene to preserve its golden flame color; soluble in liquid water.
Stored in kerosene to stop alpha radiation; soluble in aqueous ethyl alcohol.
e: Explanation: Option 1 misstates the physical reason for storage and lists reactive acids. Option 0 is correct because Sodium reacts violently with atmospheric oxygen to form sodium oxide ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{O}$) and with air moisture to form sodium hydroxide ($\\text{NaOH}$) and hydrogen gas, releasing heat that can ignite the metal. Storing it under hydrocarbon oils like **Kerosene** creates a barrier against air and water. Furthermore, sodium is soluble in non-polar organic solvents like **Benzene ($\\text{C}_6\\text{H}_6$)**. Option 2 and Option 3 describe violent reactions with water or alcohol rather than simple solvation.

qe: Tetraethyl lead ($\\text{TEL}$) was historically synthesized as an antiknock additive for petroleum fuels. Which sodium alloy serves as a primary precursor reagent in the industrial synthesis of TEL?
qh: टेट्राएथिल लेड ($\\text{TEL}$) को ऐतिहासिक रूप से पेट्रोलियम ईंधन के लिए एंटी-नॉकिंग योज्य (antiknock additive) के रूप में संश्लेषित किया गया था। कौन सी सोडियम मिश्र धातु $\\text{TEL}$ के औद्योगिक संश्लेषण में एक प्राथमिक अग्रदूत अभिकर्मक (precursor reagent) के रूप में कार्य करती है?
o: Sodium-Amalgam alloy ($\\text{Na}-\\text{Hg}$)
Sodium-Lead alloy ($\\text{Na}-\\text{Pb}$)
Sodium-Copper alloy ($\\text{Na}-\\text{Cu}$)
Sodium-Magnesium alloy ($\\text{Na}-\\text{Mg}$)
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists sodium amalgam, which is used as a reducing agent in organic chemistry rather than for TEL synthesis. Option 1 is correct because **Tetraethyl Lead [$\\text{Pb}(\\text{C}_2\\text{H}_5)_4$, or TEL]** is synthesized industrially by reacting ethyl chloride with a **Sodium-Lead Alloy ($\\text{Na}-\\text{Pb}$)**: $4\\text{C}_2\\text{H}_5\\text{Cl} + 4\\text{Na-Pb} \\rightarrow \\text{Pb}(\\text{C}_2\\text{H}_5)_4 + 3\\text{Pb} + 4\\text{NaCl}$. This reaction uses sodium to bind chloride ions as $\\text{NaCl}$, driving the alkylation of lead. Option 2 and Option 3 list alloys that are not involved in TEL synthesis.

qe: In laboratory physical chemistry, a 'freezing mixture' can be prepared using sodium chloride and ice. What conditions and physical mechanisms govern the formation of this freezing mixture?
qh: प्रयोगशाला भौतिक रसायन विज्ञान में, सोडियम क्लोराइड और बर्फ का उपयोग करके एक 'हिमकारी मिश्रण' (freezing mixture) तैयार किया जा सकता है। कौन सी स्थितियां और भौतिक तंत्र इस हिमकारी मिश्रण के निर्माण को नियंत्रित करते हैं?
o: Mixing $\\text{NaCl}$ with ice at high pressures and temperatures above $100^\\circ\\text{C}$ to boil the mixture.
Mixing $\\text{NaCl}$ with ice at lower pressure and moderate temperature, causing depression of the freezing point.
Mixing $\\text{NaCl}$ with pure sodium metal under absolute vacuum to trigger nuclear fission.
Dissolving $\\text{NaCl}$ in liquid ammonia at boiling point to evaporate all water.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes high-temperature boiling, which prevents freezing. Option 1 is correct because when **Sodium Chloride ($\\text{NaCl}$)** is mixed with ice at moderate temperatures and low pressure, the salt dissolves in the thin layer of surface water on the ice. This causes **Freezing Point Depression** [a colligative property where dissolving a non-volatile solute lowers the temperature at which the solvent freezes]. The system absorbs heat from its surroundings to melt the ice and dissolve the salt, dropping the mixture's temperature down to $-21^\\circ\\text{C}$ ($252\\text{ K}$) and creating a **Freezing Mixture**. Option 2 and Option 3 introduce nuclear or liquid-ammonia distractors.

qe: Sodium Hydroxide ($\\text{NaOH}$) is an important alkali produced in the chemical industry. What is its common commercial name, and what are its primary industrial applications?
qh: सोडियम हाइड्रोक्साइड ($\\text{NaOH}$) रासायनिक उद्योग में उत्पादित एक महत्वपूर्ण क्षार है। इसका सामान्य वाणिज्यिक नाम क्या है, और इसके प्राथमिक औद्योगिक अनुप्रयोग क्या हैं?
o: Baking Soda; used as a leavening agent in baking.
Caustic Soda; used in soap and detergent manufacturing, pH regulation, petroleum refining, and sodium extraction.
Washing Soda; used exclusively to soften permanent water hardness.
Quicklime; used for white-washing building walls.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies baking soda ($\\text{NaHCO}_3$). Option 1 is correct because **Sodium Hydroxide ($\\text{NaOH}$)** is commercially known as **Caustic Soda**. It is a strong, highly corrosive deliquescent base used industrially for: saponification in **Soaps and Detergents Manufacturing**, regulating pH in chemical processing, refining petroleum products, and as an electrolyte in the industrial extraction of sodium metal via Castner's process. Option 2 identifies washing soda ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{CO}_3 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$), and Option 3 identifies quicklime ($\\text{CaO}$).

qe: Solid sodium hydroxide pellets ($\\text{NaOH}$) left exposed to ambient air turn into a liquid film and eventually transform into a dry white powder. What sequence of chemical reactions drives this transformation?
qh: सॉलिड सोडियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड छर्रे ($\\text{NaOH}$) खुली हवा में छोड़े जाने पर एक तरल फिल्म में बदल जाते हैं और अंततः एक सूखे सफेद पाउडर में परिवर्तित हो जाते हैं। रासायनिक प्रतिक्रियाओं का कौन सा क्रम इस परिवर्तन को संचालित करता है?
o: $\\text{NaOH}$ undergoes rapid sub-surface reduction to yield metallic sodium powder.
$\\text{NaOH}$ absorbs atmospheric moisture via deliquescence, then absorbs atmospheric $\\text{CO}_2$ to form sodium carbonate ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{CO}_3$), which effloresces into a dry powder.
$\\text{NaOH}$ reacts with atmospheric nitrogen gas to synthesize insoluble sodamide powder.
$\\text{NaOH}$ sublimes directly into volatile gaseous oxides, leaving an inert silica residue.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies the reaction as a reduction to metallic sodium, which cannot occur in moist air. Option 1 is correct because solid **Sodium Hydroxide ($\\text{NaOH}$)** is a highly **Deliquescent** substance [a material that absorbs sufficient moisture from the atmosphere to dissolve completely in that absorbed water, forming a liquid solution]. Once dissolved in this water film, $\\text{NaOH}$ absorbs atmospheric carbon dioxide gas ($\\text{CO}_2$), triggering a neutralization reaction that produces hydrated **Sodium Carbonate ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{CO}_3 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$)**: $2\\text{NaOH} + \\text{CO}_2 \\rightarrow \\text{Na}_2\\text{CO}_3 + \\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. As this sodium carbonate stands in dry air, it undergoes **Efflorescence** [the spontaneous loss of water of crystallization from a hydrated salt when exposed to air], crumbling into a fine white anhydrous or monohydrated soda powder. Option 2 describes an impossible reaction with unreactive nitrogen gas, and Option 3 proposes a physical sublimation process that does not occur for sodium hydroxide.

qe: In photographic film processing, Sodium Thiosulphate ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{S}_2\\text{O}_3 \\cdot 5\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$, commonly known as 'Hypo') acts as a fixing agent. What specific chemical role does Hypo perform during this process?
qh: फोटोग्राफिक फिल्म प्रोसेसिंग में, सोडियम थायोसल्फेट ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{S}_2\\text{O}_3 \\cdot 5\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$, जिसे आमतौर पर 'हाइपो' कहा जाता है) एक फिक्सिंग एजेंट के रूप में कार्य करता है। इस प्रक्रिया के दौरान हाइपो कौन सी विशिष्ट रासायनिक भूमिका निभाता है?
o: It oxidizes metallic silver into dark silver nitrate particles.
It dissolves and removes light-exposed, un-decomposed Silver Bromide ($\\text{AgBr}$) from the film as a soluble silver thiosulphate complex salt.
It acts as a drying agent that solidifies gelatin layers into glass.
It converts liquid water into volatile chlorine gas to bleach the background.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly states that hypo oxidizes metallic silver, whereas metallic silver actually forms the dark image that hypo preserves. Option 1 is correct because **Sodium Thiosulphate ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{S}_2\\text{O}_3 \\cdot 5\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$)** serves as a **Fixing Agent** [a chemical solution that stabilizes photographic prints by dissolving unreduced halide salts]. During film exposure and development, un-decomposed silver bromide ($\\text{AgBr}$) remains on the light-sensitive emulsion. Hypo reacts with this un-decomposed $\\text{AgBr}$ to convert it into a water-soluble coordination complex, Sodium Dithiosulphatoargentate(I) [$\\text{Na}_3[\\text{Ag}(\\text{S}_2\\text{O}_3)_2]$], which is easily washed away, preventing the remaining film from darkening when exposed to light. Option 2 describes a mechanical drying function, and Option 3 claims it releases chlorine gas (hypo actually acts as an anti-chlor to remove excess chlorine).

qe: Microcosmic salt [$\\text{Na}(\\text{NH}_4)\\text{HPO}_4 \\cdot 4\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$] is utilized in qualitative inorganic analysis for the microcosmic salt bead test. What thermal decomposition products are liberated when this salt is strongly heated on a platinum wire loop?
qh: माइक्रोकोस्मिक साल्ट [$\\text{Na}(\\text{NH}_4)\\text{HPO}_4 \\cdot 4\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$] का उपयोग गुणात्मक अकार्बनिक विश्लेषण में माइक्रोकोस्मिक साल्ट बीड परीक्षण के लिए किया जाता है। जब इस लवण को प्लैटिनम वायर लूप पर तेजी से गर्म किया जाता है तो कौन से तापीय अपघटन उत्पाद (thermal decomposition products) मुक्त होते हैं?
o: Sodium carbonate, nitrogen gas, and pure metallic sodium.
Sodium metaphosphate ($\\text{NaPO}_3$), ammonia gas ($\\text{NH}_3$), and water vapor.
Glauber's salt, nitric acid fumes, and phosphorus pentoxide.
Sodium hydride, hydrogen gas, and free nitrogen peroxide.
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists metallic sodium, which cannot form from heating phosphate salts. Option 1 is correct because **Microcosmic Salt** (chemically **Sodium Ammonium Hydrogen Phosphate Tetrahydrate**, $\\text{Na}(\\text{NH}_4)\\text{HPO}_4 \\cdot 4\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) undergoes a multi-stage thermal decomposition when heated strongly on a platinum loop. It first loses its water of crystallization, then splits into gaseous **Ammonia ($\\text{NH}_3$)** and water vapor, leaving behind a transparent, glass-like bead of **Sodium Metaphosphate ($\\text{NaPO}_3$)**: $\\text{Na}(\\text{NH}_4)\\text{HPO}_4 \\cdot 4\\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\xrightarrow{\\Delta} \\text{NaPO}_3 + \\text{NH}_3\\uparrow + 5\\text{H}_2\\text{O}\\uparrow$. This metaphosphate bead reacts with transition metal cations to form colored orthophosphate beads, serving as a diagnostic qualitative test. Option 2 and Option 3 list incorrect acid or hydride gas decomposition products.

qe: Magnesium occurs in nature as several economically vital mineral ores. Which choice correctly coordinates the mineral ore name with its precise chemical formula?
qh: मैग्नीशियम प्रकृति में कई आर्थिक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण खनिज अयस्कों के रूप में होता है। कौन सा विकल्प खनिज अयस्क के नाम को उसके सटीक रासायनिक सूत्र के साथ सही ढंग से समन्वित करता है?
o: Dolomite: $\\text{MgSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$; Magnesite: $\\text{MgCl}_2 \\cdot \\text{KCl} \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$

Magnesite: $\\text{MgCO}_3$; Dolomite: $\\text{MgCO}_3 \\cdot \\text{CaCO}_3$; Epsomite: $\\text{MgSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$; Carnallite: $\\text{MgCl}_2 \\cdot \\text{KCl} \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$
Magnesite: $\\text{CaCO}_3$; Carnallite: $\\text{MgSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$
Epsomite: $\\text{MgCO}_3 \\cdot \\text{CaCO}_3$; Dolomite: $\\text{MgCl}_2 \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$
e: Explanation: Option 0 swaps the chemical formulas of Epsomite and Carnallite onto Dolomite and Magnesite. Option 1 is correct because the principal natural mineral ores of magnesium are: **Magnesite** (Magnesium Carbonate, $\\text{MgCO}_3$), **Dolomite** (Double Carbonate of Magnesium and Calcium, $\\text{MgCO}_3 \\cdot \\text{CaCO}_3$), **Epsomite / Epsom Salt** (Hydrated Magnesium Sulphate, $\\text{MgSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$), and **Carnallite** (Double Chloride of Magnesium and Potassium, $\\text{MgCl}_2 \\cdot \\text{KCl} \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$). Option 2 misidentifies pure calcium carbonate as magnesite, and Option 3 scrambles double salts.

qe: Magnesium ribbon is a highly reactive metal strip used in laboratory syntheses. To prevent premature oxidation or degradation during storage, in what specific atmospheric environment is magnesium ribbon stored?
qh: मैग्नीशियम रिबन एक अत्यधिक प्रतिक्रियाशील धातु की पट्टी है जिसका उपयोग प्रयोगशाला संश्लेषण में किया जाता है। भंडारण के दौरान समय से पहले ऑक्सीकरण या क्षरण को रोकने के लिए, मैग्नीशियम रिबन को किस विशिष्ट वायुमंडलीय वातावरण में रखा जाता है?
o: In an atmosphere of concentrated oxygen gas to build a waxy cuticle.
In an atmosphere of inert nitrogen gas to shield the reactive metal surface.
Submerged in pure liquid water saturated with carbon dioxide.
In a open container filled with volatile chlorine vapors.
e: Explanation: Option 0 proposes storing the metal in oxygen, which would rapidly oxidize it into magnesium oxide. Option 1 is correct because magnesium metal reacts readily with atmospheric oxygen and moisture at ambient conditions, forming a dull surface coating of oxide and hydroxide. To maintain its unreacted metallic state, magnesium ribbon is stored in a dry, inert **Nitrogen Atmosphere** ($\\text{N}_2$). Nitrogen acts as a protective blanket because its strong $\\text{N}\\equiv\\text{N}$ triple bond resists chemical reaction with solid magnesium at room temperature. Option 2 introduces water, which reacts with magnesium, and Option 3 introduces corrosive chlorine gas.

qe: Grignard reagents are widely used organometallic compounds in organic chemistry synthesis. Under what specific reaction conditions is a Grignard reagent prepared, and what chemical formula defines it?
qh: ग्रिग्नार्ड अभिकर्मक (Grignard reagents) कार्बनिक रसायन विज्ञान संश्लेषण में व्यापक रूप से उपयोग किए जाने वाले ऑर्गनोमेटैलिक यौगिक हैं। ग्रिग्नार्ड अभिकर्मक किस विशिष्ट प्रतिक्रिया स्थितियों के तहत तैयार किया जाता है, और कौन सा रासायनिक सूत्र इसे परिभाषित करता है?
o: Reacting magnesium with alkyl halides in the presence of water; formula: $\\text{Mg(OH)}X$
Reacting magnesium metal with an alkyl halide ($\\text{RX}$) in the presence of dry ether; formula: $\\text{RMgX}$
Boiling magnesium carbonate with alcohol under high pressure; formula: $\\text{R}_2\\text{Mg}$
Reacting magnesium chloride with sodium hydroxide; formula: $\\text{NaMgX}_3$
e: Explanation: Option 0 includes water, which hydrolyzes and destroys Grignard reagents instantly into alkanes. Option 1 is correct because a **Grignard Reagent** is an organometallic compound prepared by reacting magnesium turnings with an **Alkyl Halide ($\\text{RX}$)** or aryl halide in an **Anhydrous Dry Ether Solvent**: $\\text{R-X} + \\text{Mg} \\xrightarrow{\\text{Dry Ether}} \\text{R-Mg-X}$ [where R is an alkyl/aryl group and X is a halogen atom like Cl, Br, or I]. The ether solvent acts as a Lewis base, stabilizing the organomagnesium complex. Option 2 and Option 3 list inorganic salts or methods that do not produce Grignard reagents.

qe: Lightweight alloys are essential materials in modern aeronautical and automotive engineering. What is the composition of the magnesium alloy 'Elektron', and what mechanical property makes it valuable for aircraft frames?
qh: हल्के मिश्र धातु आधुनिक वैमानिकी और ऑटोमोटिव इंजीनियरिंग में आवश्यक सामग्री हैं। मैग्नीशियम मिश्र धातु 'इलेक्ट्रॉन' (Elektron) की संरचना क्या है, और कौन सा यांत्रिक गुण इसे विमान के फ्रेम के लिए मूल्यवान बनाता है?
o: $\\text{Mg}\\ (5\\%), \\text{Al}\\ (90\\%), \\text{Cu}\\ (5\\%)$; extremely heavy and brittle.
$\\text{Mg}\\ (95\\%), \\text{Zn}\\ (4.5\\%), \\text{Cu}\\ (0.5\\%)$; remarkably light, soft, and high in strength-to-weight ratio.
$\\text{Mg}\\ (50\\%), \\text{Pb}\\ (50\\%)$; highly flexible liquid metal.
$\\text{Mg}\\ (10\\%), \\text{Hg}\\ (90\\%)$; liquid amalgam used in nuclear rods.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misstates the primary metal component as aluminium. Option 1 is correct because **Elektron** is a high-performance, lightweight **Magnesium Alloy** composed of **95% Magnesium ($\\text{Mg}$), 4.5% Zinc ($\\text{Zn}$), and 0.5% Copper ($\\text{Cu}$)**. Because magnesium is one of the lightest structural metals, alloying it with zinc and copper increases its tensile strength without significantly adding mass. This yields a material with a high strength-to-weight ratio, making it useful for constructing aircraft frames and motor vehicle engine casings. Option 2 and Option 3 describe heavy lead alloys or mercury amalgams.

qe: Magnesium Carbonate occurs naturally as magnesite. What is the specific chemical formula of the medicinal/cosmetic compound known as 'Magnesium Alba', and what are its main applications?
qh: मैग्नीशियम कार्बोनेट स्वाभाविक रूप से मैग्नेसाइट के रूप में होता है। 'मैग्नीशियम अल्बा' (Magnesium Alba) के रूप में जाने जाने वाले औषधीय/सौंदर्य प्रसाधन यौगिक का विशिष्ट रासायनिक सूत्र क्या है, और इसके मुख्य अनुप्रयोग क्या हैं?
o: \\text{MgSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}; used as a high-temperature metallurgical flux.
2\\text{MgCO}_3 \\cdot \\text{Mg(OH)}_2 \\cdot 3\\text{H}_2\\text{O}; used as an antacid medicine, dental abrasive in toothpastes, and in cosmetics.
\\text{MgCl}_2 \\cdot 5\\text{MgO} \\cdot n\\text{H}_2\\text{O}; used to weld railway tracks.
\\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2; used as an explosive photographic propellant.
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists Epsom salt, which is a sulphate rather than a hydrated basic carbonate. Option 1 is correct because **Magnesium Alba** is a hydrated basic magnesium carbonate compound with the formula **$2\\text{MgCO}_3 \\cdot \\text{Mg(OH)}_2 \\cdot 3\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$**. It serves as a mild alkaline drug to neutralize stomach hyperacidity (antacid), acts as a mild **Dental Abrasive** in toothpaste formulations to clean plaque without damaging enamel, and is used as an absorbent filler in cosmetics. Option 2 lists Sorel cement, and Option 3 lists magnesium nitrate.

qe: Sorel Cement is a rapid-setting, high-strength binding material used in specialized dental and industrial applications. What is its chemical composition, and how is it prepared?
qh: सोरेल सीमेंट (Sorel Cement) एक त्वरित-सेटिंग, उच्च-शक्ति बाध्यकारी सामग्री है जिसका उपयोग विशिष्ट दंत चिकित्सा और औद्योगिक अनुप्रयोगों में किया जाता है। इसकी रासायनिक संरचना क्या है, और इसे कैसे तैयार किया जाता है?
o: \\text{CaSO}_4 \\cdot \\frac{1}{2}\\text{H}_2\\text{O}; prepared by heating gypsum at $373\\text{ K}$.

\\text{MgCl}_2 \\cdot 5\\text{MgO} \\cdot n\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$ (Magnesium Oxychloride); prepared by mixing calcined magnesium oxide ($\\text{MgO}$) with a concentrated aqueous solution of magnesium chloride ($\\text{MgCl}_2$).
\\text{Na}_2\\text{CO}_3 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$; prepared by recrystallizing soda ash.
\\text{CaO} \\cdot \\text{SiO}_2$; prepared by slaking quicklime with carbonated water.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes Plaster of Paris, a calcium compound. Option 1 is correct because **Sorel Cement** (chemically **Magnesium Oxychloride Cement**) has the basic formula **$\\text{MgCl}_2 \\cdot 5\\text{MgO} \\cdot n\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$**. It is prepared by mixing powdered calcined magnesia (Magnesium Oxide, $\\text{MgO}$) with a concentrated solution of **Magnesium Chloride ($\\text{MgCl}_2$)**. The mixture sets into a hard, dense, porcelain-like mass, making it useful for dental fillings, cementing glass and porcelain, and manufacturing artificial stone floorings. Option 2 lists washing soda, and Option 3 describes calcium silicate mortar.

qe: Calcium is an s-block element located in Group-2 and Period-4 of the Modern Periodic Table. What is its electronic configuration, and who first isolated it in its pure metallic form in 1808?
qh: कैल्शियम आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी के समूह-2 और आवर्त-4 में स्थित एक s-ब्लॉक तत्व है। इसका इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास क्या है, और किसने 1808 में इसे इसके शुद्ध धात्विक रूप में सबसे पहले अलग (isolate) किया था?
o: Configuration: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2$; Isolated by Dmitri Mendeléev.
Configuration: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2$; Isolated by Humphry Davy.
Configuration: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^1$; Isolated by Henry Moseley.
Configuration: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2$; Isolated by John Newlands.
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists magnesium's electronic configuration ($n=3$) and misattributes isolation to Mendeléev. Option 1 is correct because Calcium ($\\text{Ca}$, $Z=20$, atomic mass $\\approx 40\\text{ u}$) has the ground-state **Electronic Configuration** $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2$ (or $[\\text{Ar}]4s^2$). Pure elemental calcium was first isolated in 1808 by English chemist **Humphry Davy** via the electrolytic decomposition of a moist lime-mercuric oxide mixture. Option 2 lists sodium's configuration, and Option 3 lists zinc's configuration.

qe:
Industrial extraction of pure metallic calcium relies on the electrolytic reduction of fused anhydrous Calcium Chloride ($
\text{CaCl}_2$). Why is Fluorspar ($
\text{CaF}_2$) added to the electrolyte bath during this process?
qh: शुद्ध धात्विक कैल्शियम का औद्योगिक निष्कर्षण संगलित निर्जल कैल्शियम क्लोराइड ($\\text{CaCl}_2$) के इलेक्ट्रोलाइटिक अपचयन पर निर्भर करता है। इस प्रक्रिया के दौरान इलेक्ट्रोलाइट बाथ में फ्लोरास्पार ($\\text{CaF}_2$) क्यों मिलाया जाता है?
o: To act as an oxidizing agent that converts free calcium metal into a volatile nitrate gas.
To lower the melting point of anhydrous $\\text{CaCl}_2$ and improve the electrical conductivity of the molten bath.
To elevate the bath temperature to $3000\\text{ K}$ to evaporate impurities.
To bind calcium ions as an insoluble sludge at the anode.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies fluorspar as an oxidizing agent, which would destroy the extracted metal. Option 1 is correct because pure anhydrous calcium chloride ($\\text{CaCl}_2$) has a high melting point ($\\sim 772^\\circ\\text{C}$ or $1045\\text{ K}$). Electrolyzing it at this temperature is energy-intensive and can cause extracted calcium metal to vaporize or dissolve back into the bath. Adding **Fluorspar (Calcium Fluoride, $\\text{CaF}_2$)** in a ratio of about 85% $\\text{CaCl}_2$ to 15% $\\text{CaF}_2$ acts as a **Fluxing Agent** [a chemical substance added to lower the melting temperature and reduce viscosity of a molten salt mixture], lowering the fusion temperature and increasing electrical conductivity for efficient electrolytic reduction. Option 2 and Option 3 describe elevated temperatures or sludge formation.

qe:
Calcium chloride ($
\text{CaCl}_2$) is an important salt used as a drying agent. In which major industrial process is $
\text{CaCl}_2$ produced as a major chemical by-product?
qh: कैल्शियम क्लोराइड ($\\text{CaCl}_2$) एक महत्वपूर्ण लवण है जिसका उपयोग सुखाने वाले एजेंट (drying agent) के रूप में किया जाता है। किस प्रमुख औद्योगिक प्रक्रिया में $\\text{CaCl}_2$ एक प्रमुख रासायनिक उप-उत्पाद (by-product) के रूप में निर्मित होता है?
o: Castner's Process for sodium extraction.
Solvay Process for the manufacture of Sodium Carbonate ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{CO}_3$).
Down's Process for molten salt electrolysis.
Haber's Process for ammonia synthesis.
e: Explanation: Option 0 is Castner's process, which yields sodium, oxygen, and water, not calcium chloride. Option 1 is correct because in the **Solvay Process** (ammonia-soda process) for manufacturing washing soda, carbon dioxide is passed through brine saturated with ammonia. During the regeneration of ammonia, slaked lime [$\\text{Ca(OH)}_2$] is reacted with ammonium chloride solution: $2\\text{NH}_4\\text{Cl} + \\text{Ca(OH)}_2 \\rightarrow 2\\text{NH}_3 + \\text{CaCl}_2 + 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. The resulting **Calcium Chloride ($\\text{CaCl}_2$)** is recovered as a major industrial by-product. Option 2 produces sodium and chlorine, and Option 3 synthesizes ammonia gas.

qe: Metallic calcium is used as a chemical reagent in metallurgical and purification processes. Which option correctly identifies two primary chemical uses of metallic calcium?
qh: धात्विक कैल्शियम का उपयोग धातुकर्म और शोधन प्रक्रियाओं में एक रासायनिक अभिकर्मक के रूप में किया जाता है। कौन सा विकल्प धात्विक कैल्शियम के दो प्राथमिक रासायनिक उपयोगों की सही पहचान करता है?
o: As a neutron moderator in nuclear reactors and as a food preservative in vinegar.
As a dehydrating agent for preparing absolute alcohol and as a scavenger/deoxidizer to remove last traces of air/oxygen from cast iron, steel, and high vacuum systems.
As a primary dye in textile printing and as a component of soda-acid fire extinguishers.
As an ingredient in antacid tablets and as a bleaching agent in paper mills.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misassigns nuclear moderator and food preservative roles to calcium metal. Option 1 is correct because metallic calcium is an active reducing agent with a strong affinity for water, oxygen, and nitrogen. It is used as a **Dehydrating Agent** to remove trace water from $95\\%$ ethanol to produce pure **Absolute Alcohol** ($100\\% \\text{ C}_2\\text{H}_5\\text{OH}$). It also functions as a **Scavenger/Deoxidizer** in metallurgy to scrub trace oxygen, sulfur, and nitrogen gases from molten cast iron, steel, and copper, and to produce high vacuums in specialized glass tubes. Option 2 and Option 3 describe uses belonging to baking soda, bleaching powder, or milk of magnesia.

qe:
When water is added to Quicklime ($
\text{CaO}$), a vigorous exothermic reaction occurs accompanied by a characteristic hissing sound. What chemical product forms, and what is this process called?
qh: जब बिना बुझे चूने (Quicklime, $\\text{CaO}$) में पानी मिलाया जाता है, तो एक विशिष्ट हिसिंग (hissing) ध्वनि के साथ एक तीव्र ऊष्माक्षेपी प्रतिक्रिया होती है। कौन सा रासायनिक उत्पाद बनता है, और इस प्रक्रिया को क्या कहा जाता है?
o: Calcium carbonate; process is called Calcination.
Calcium hydroxide [$\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, Slaked Lime]; process is called Slaking of Lime.
Calcium sulphate; process is called Gypsum Plastering.
Calcium carbide; process is called Carbonation.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies the product as calcium carbonate and names calcination, which involves heating carbonate ores. Option 1 is correct because adding water to **Quicklime (Calcium Oxide, $\\text{CaO}$)** triggers a highly exothermic hydration reaction: $\\text{CaO} + \\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\rightarrow \\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \\text{Heat}$. The rapid release of heat boils local moisture, producing a steam release accompanied by a crackling/hissing sound. This reaction yields **Slaked Lime [Calcium Hydroxide, $\\text{Ca(OH)}_2$]**, and the process is formally termed the **Slaking of Lime**. Option 2 and Option 3 describe gypsum formation or carbide manufacturing.

qe:
Slaked lime [$
\text{Ca(OH)}_2$] forms distinct aqueous states depending on its concentration and state of suspension. What terms define a clear filtered aqueous solution versus a thick suspension of slaked lime in water?
qh: बुझा हुआ चूना [$\text{Ca(OH)}_2$] अपनी सांद्रता और निलंबन की स्थिति के आधार पर अलग-अलग जलीय अवस्थाएँ बनाता है। पानी में बुझे हुए चूने के स्पष्ट फ़िल्टर किए गए जलीय घोल बनाम एक मोटे निलंबन (thick suspension) को कौन से शब्द परिभाषित करते हैं?
o: Clear solution: Milk of Lime; Thick suspension: Lime Water.
Clear solution: Lime Water; Thick suspension: Milk of Lime.
Clear solution: Soda Lime; Thick suspension: Quicklime.
Clear solution: Sorel Cement; Thick suspension: Gypsum.
e: Explanation: Option 0 reverses the specific chemical terminology for the solution versus the suspension. Option 1 is correct because Calcium Hydroxide [$\\text{Ca(OH)}_2$] is sparingly soluble in water. A clear, filtered saturated aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide is known as **Lime Water** (used to test for $\\text{CO}_2$ gas, which turns it milky due to $\\text{CaCO}_3$ precipitation). In contrast, a thick, milky white suspension of slaked lime particles dispersed in water is called **Milk of Lime** (used as a industrial alkaline wash and in whitewashing). Option 2 lists soda lime (a dry mixture of $\\text{NaOH}$ and $\\text{CaO}$), and Option 3 lists cement and plaster compounds.

qe: Soda Lime is a solid alkaline reagent used in laboratory gas absorption and organic decarboxylation reactions. How is Soda Lime prepared?
qh: सोडा लाइम (Soda Lime) प्रयोगशाला गैस अवशोषण और कार्बनिक डीकार्बोक्सिलेशन प्रतिक्रियाओं में उपयोग किया जाने वाला एक ठोस क्षारीय अभिकर्मक है। सोडा लाइम कैसे तैयार किया जाता है?
o: By slaking sodium metal with pure sulphuric acid.
By slaking Quicklime ($\\text{CaO}$) with a concentrated solution of Caustic Soda ($\\text{NaOH}$).
By boiling calcium carbonate with ammonia gas.
By reacting Glauber's salt with slaked lime.
e: Explanation: Option 0 involves acid reactions that do not form alkalis. Option 1 is correct because **Soda Lime** is a porous granular solid mixture prepared by slaking **Quicklime (Calcium Oxide, $\\text{CaO}$)** with an aqueous solution of **Caustic Soda (Sodium Hydroxide, $\\text{NaOH}$)**, followed by drying. The resulting solid consists primarily of $\\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, $\\text{NaOH}$, and $\\text{CaO}$. The inclusion of $\\text{CaO}$ prevents the $\\text{NaOH}$ from deliquescing into a liquid, keeping the reagent as an easy-to-handle solid that absorbs $\\text{CO}_2$ and moisture gas streams. Option 2 and Option 3 describe irrelevant chemical combinations.

qe:
Bleaching Powder ($
\text{CaOCl}_2$) is an industrial disinfectant and bleaching agent. What specific starting materials and reaction conditions are required for its manufacture?
qh: ब्लीचिंग पाउडर ($\\text{CaOCl}_2$) एक औद्योगिक कीटाणुनाशक और ब्लीचिंग एजेंट है। इसके निर्माण के लिए किन विशिष्ट प्रारंभिक सामग्रियों और प्रतिक्रिया स्थितियों की आवश्यकता होती है?
o: Passing carbon dioxide gas over wet quicklime at $1000\\text{ K}$.
Passing chlorine gas ($\\text{Cl}_2$) over dry slaked lime [$\\text{Ca(OH)}_2$] at room temperature.
Boiling calcium carbonate with concentrated hydrochloric acid.
Electrolyzing an aqueous solution of calcium sulphate.
e: Explanation: Option 0 uses carbon dioxide instead of chlorine, which yields limestone instead of bleaching powder. Option 1 is correct because **Bleaching Powder** (Calcium Oxychloride, $\\text{CaOCl}_2$) is manufactured by passing elemental **Chlorine Gas ($\\text{Cl}_2$)** over **Dry Slaked Lime [$\\text{Ca(OH)}_2$]**: $\\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \\text{Cl}_2 \\rightarrow \\text{CaOCl}_2 + \\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. Moisture must be minimized to prevent secondary hydrolysis of the product. Option 2 yields calcium chloride solution with $\\text{CO}_2$ gas release, and Option 3 electrolyzes gypsum.

qe:
Calcium Carbonate ($
\text{CaCO}_3$) occurs naturally in diverse geological and biological forms. What thermal decomposition reaction occurs when $
\text{CaCO}_3$ is heated above $1200
\text{ K}$ in a lime kiln?
qh: कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट ($\\text{CaCO}_3$) स्वाभाविक रूप से विविध भूवैज्ञानिक और जैविक रूपों में होता है। चूने की भट्टी (lime kiln) में $\\text{CaCO}_3$ को $1200\\text{ K}$ से ऊपर गर्म करने पर कौन सी तापीय अपघटन प्रतिक्रिया होती है?
o: It decomposes into metallic calcium and ozone gas.
It decomposes into Quicklime ($\\text{CaO}$) and Carbon Dioxide gas ($\\text{CO}_2$).
It transforms into slaked lime and carbon monoxide gas.
It undergoes sublimation into calcium hydride vapor.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes an impossible decomposition that yields ozone. Option 1 is correct because **Calcium Carbonate ($\\text{CaCO}_3$)** (found naturally as limestone, chalk, marble, and pearl) is thermally stable at ambient conditions, but undergoes **Thermal Decomposition** when heated to high temperatures ($\\sim 1200\\text{ K}$ or $900^\\circ\\text{C}$) in a lime kiln: $\\text{CaCO}_3 \\xrightarrow{\\Delta} \\text{CaO} + \\text{CO}_2\\uparrow$. This reversible endothermic reaction drives off carbon dioxide gas, leaving solid **Quicklime (Calcium Oxide, $\\text{CaO}$)**. Option 2 and Option 3 describe incorrect hydration or sublimation pathways.

qe:
Milk of Magnesia [$
\text{Mg(OH)}_2$] is a widely used pharmaceutical suspension. What primary physiological conditions is it prescribed to treat, and what chemical mechanism governs its action?
qh: मिल्क ऑफ मैग्नेशिया [$\\text{Mg(OH)}_2$] एक व्यापक रूप से इस्तेमाल किया जाने वाला फार्मास्युटिकल निलंबन है। इसका इलाज करने के लिए किन प्राथमिक शारीरिक स्थितियों के लिए निर्धारित किया जाता है, और कौन सा रासायनिक तंत्र इसके कार्य को नियंत्रित करता है?
o: Treats low blood pressure by releasing sodium ions into the bloodstream.
Treats stomach hyperacidity as an antacid and constipation as a laxative by neutralizing excess gastric $\\text{HCl}$ without causing systemic alkalosis.
Treats kidney stones by dissolving calcium hydroxyapatite into volatile nitrogen gas.
Treats bone fractures by binding directly to collagen fibers.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies sodium functions and blood pressure regulation. Option 1 is correct because **Milk of Magnesia** is an aqueous suspension of **Magnesium Hydroxide [$\\text{Mg(OH)}_2$]**. Because $\\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is sparingly soluble, it acts as a mild, non-systemic **Antacid** that neutralizes excess stomach hydrochloric acid ($\\text{HCl}$): $\\text{Mg(OH)}_2 + 2\\text{HCl} \\rightarrow \\text{MgCl}_2 + 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. Its low solubility prevents the rapid absorption of hydroxide ions into the bloodstream, avoiding systemic alkalosis. In higher doses, the unabsorbed magnesium ions retain water in the intestinal lumen via osmosis, acting as a saline **Laxative**. It is also used to treat scalp dandruff. Option 2 and Option 3 describe impossible kidney stone or collagen binding claims.

qe:
Epsom salt ($
\text{MgSO}_4 \cdot 7
\text{H}_2
\text{O}$) exhibits a specific crystallographic relationship with White Vitriol ($
\text{ZnSO}_4 \cdot 7
\text{H}_2
\text{O}$). What crystallographic term defines this structural relationship, and what physical property causes Epsom salt to lose its crystal shape in dry air?
qh: एप्सम साल्ट ($\\text{MgSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) व्हाइट विट्रियोल ($\\text{ZnSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) के साथ एक विशिष्ट क्रिस्टलोग्राफिक संबंध प्रदर्शित करता है। कौन सा क्रिस्टलोग्राफिक शब्द इस संरचनात्मक संबंध को परिभाषित करता है, और कौन सा भौतिक गुण एप्सम साल्ट को शुष्क हवा में अपने क्रिस्टल आकार को खोने का कारण बनता है?
o: Allotropic; Deliquescence.
Isomorphous; Efflorescence.
Amphoteric; Passivation.
Polymorphic; Hygroscopy.
e: Explanation: Option 0 uses allotropic (which applies to elements) and deliquescence (absorbing water). Option 1 is correct because **Epsom Salt ($\\text{MgSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$)** and **White Vitriol ($\\text{ZnSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$)** are **Isomorphous** [compounds that possess identical crystalline structures and unit cell geometries with similar chemical formulas]. When exposed to dry air, hydrated magnesium sulphate undergoes **Efflorescence** [the spontaneous loss of water of crystallization to the atmosphere], crumbling into a lower-hydrate or anhydrous white powder and losing its defined crystal shape. Option 2 and Option 3 introduce amphoteric or polymorphic terms incorrectly.

qe: Calcium chloride ($\\text{CaCl}_2$) is widely used as an industrial drying agent due to its hygroscopic and deliquescent nature. However, it cannot be used to dry gases like alcohol vapor or ammonia. What chemical phenomenon prevents its use for drying these specific substances?
qh: कैल्शियम क्लोराइड ($\\text{CaCl}_2$) अपने आर्द्रताग्राही और प्रस्वेद्य स्वभाव के कारण औद्योगिक शुष्कन एजेंट के रूप में व्यापक रूप से उपयोग किया जाता है। हालाँकि, इसका उपयोग अल्कोहल वाष्प या अमोनिया जैसी गैसों को सुखाने के लिए नहीं किया जा सकता है। कौन सी रासायनिक घटना इन विशिष्ट पदार्थों को सुखाने के लिए इसके उपयोग को रोकती है?
o: It oxidizes alcohol and ammonia into explosive nitrogen oxides.
It reacts chemically with alcohol and ammonia to form solid addition products (coordination complexes).
It reduces ammonia into elemental nitrogen gas while absorbing latent heat.
It undergoes rapid thermal decomposition when exposed to volatile organic vapors.
e: Explanation: Option 0 mischaracterizes calcium chloride as an oxidizing agent, which it is not. Option 1 is correct because **Calcium Chloride ($\\text{CaCl}_2$)** acts as a Lewis acid and forms stable **Addition Products** [coordination complexes where guest donor molecules bind directly to the metal salt crystal lattice] with electron-donor molecules. Specifically, it reacts with ammonia to form $\\text{CaCl}_2 \\cdot 8\\text{NH}_3$ and with ethyl alcohol to form $\\text{CaCl}_2 \\cdot 4\\text{C}_2\\text{H}_5\\text{OH}$. Instead of removing moisture, the drying agent itself chemically absorbs and reacts with the target alcohol or ammonia stream. Option 2 describes an impossible reduction pathway, and Option 3 proposes an incorrect thermal breakdown.

qe: When Plaster of Paris ($\\text{CaSO}_4 \\cdot \\frac{1}{2}\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) is mixed with water, it sets into a hard solid mass within minutes. What chemical compound is formed during this setting reaction, and what thermodynamic behavior accompanies it?
qh: जब प्लास्टर ऑफ पेरिस ($\\text{CaSO}_4 \\cdot \\frac{1}{2}\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) में पानी मिलाया जाता है, तो यह कुछ ही मिनटों में एक कठोर ठोस द्रव्यमान में जम जाता है। इस सेटिंग प्रतिक्रिया के दौरान कौन सा रासायनिक यौगिक बनता है, और इसके साथ कौन सा ऊष्मागतिकी व्यवहार होता है?
o: Converts into Anhydrite ($\\text{CaSO}_4$); highly endothermic reaction that absorbs ambient thermal energy.
Rehydrates into Gypsum ($\\text{CaSO}_4 \\cdot 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$); exothermic reaction that liberates heat, raising the mixture temperature.
Decomposes into Calcium Oxide ($\\text{CaO}$) and sulfur dioxide gas; athermic process.
Transforms into Super Phosphate of Lime; endothermic crystallization process.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly states that setting produces anhydrite via an endothermic process. Option 1 is correct because **Plaster of Paris** (Calcium Sulphate Hemihydrate, $\\text{CaSO}_4 \\cdot \\frac{1}{2}\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) undergoes **Rehydration** when mixed with water. It absorbs $1.5$ moles of water per formula unit to reform an interlocking crystalline matrix of **Gypsum ($\\text{CaSO}_4 \\cdot 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$)**: $\\text{CaSO}_4 \\cdot \\frac{1}{2}\\text{H}_2\\text{O} + 1.5\\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\rightarrow \\text{CaSO}_4 \\cdot 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. Because bond formation during hydration is an **Exothermic Process** [a chemical reaction that releases heat energy into its immediate surroundings], the temperature of the setting plaster paste noticeably rises. Option 2 and Option 3 misidentify the hydration products and thermodynamics.

qe: Fertilizers like Nitrolim ($\\text{CaCN}_2$) and Hydrolith ($\\text{CaH}_2$) serve distinct industrial and field functions. How are Nitrolim and Hydrolith synthesized or utilized according to their primary chemical properties?
qh: नाइट्रोलिम ($\\text{CaCN}_2$) और हाइड्रोलिथ ($\\text{CaH}_2$) जैसे उर्वरक/यौगिक विशिष्ट औद्योगिक और क्षेत्रीय कार्य करते हैं। नाइट्रोलिम और हाइड्रोलिथ को उनके प्राथमिक रासायनिक गुणों के अनुसार कैसे संश्लेषित या उपयोग किया जाता है?
o: Nitrolim is prepared by heating $\\text{CaC}_2$ with $\\text{N}_2$ at $2000^\\circ\\text{C}$; Hydrolith yields $\\text{H}_2$ gas upon reaction with water.
Hydrolith is prepared by burning calcium in pure nitrogen; Nitrolim releases oxygen gas when treated with cold water.
Nitrolim is a mixture of calcium phosphate and bone ash; Hydrolith is used exclusively as a dental filling.
Both Nitrolim and Hydrolith are insoluble inert ores extracted from bauxite residues.
e: Explanation: Option 1 reverses the chemical synthesis parameters and proposes incorrect gas liberation. Option 0 is correct because **Nitrolim** (Calcium Cyanamide, $\\text{CaCN}_2$, often mixed with carbon) is produced industrially by reacting calcium carbide ($\\text{CaC}_2$) with atmospheric nitrogen gas ($\\text{N}_2$) in an electric furnace at high temperatures ($\\sim 2000^\\circ\\text{C}$): $\\text{CaC}_2 + \\text{N}_2 \\rightarrow \\text{CaCN}_2 + \\text{C}$. It acts as a slow-release nitrogenous fertilizer. **Hydrolith** (Calcium Hydride, $\\text{CaH}_2$) is an ionic hydride that reacts vigorously with water to release **Hydrogen Gas ($\\text{H}_2$)**: $\\text{CaH}_2 + 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\rightarrow \\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + 2\\text{H}_2\\uparrow$, making it a portable chemical source of hydrogen. Option 2 and Option 3 misidentify superphosphate of lime or dental cements.

qe: In the metallurgy of aluminium, crude bauxite ore contains varying principal impurities. Which concentration process is deployed when bauxite contains Silica ($\\text{SiO}_2$) as its chief impurity, and what process is used when Iron Oxide ($\\text{Fe}_2\\text{O}_3$) is the chief impurity?
qh: एल्युमीनियम के धातुकर्म में, कच्चे बॉक्साइट अयस्क में विभिन्न मुख्य अशुद्धियाँ होती हैं। जब बॉक्साइट में सिलिका ($\\text{SiO}_2$) मुख्य अशुद्धि के रूप में होती है, तो कौन सी सांद्रता प्रक्रिया तैनात की जाती है, और जब आयरन ऑक्साइड ($\\text{Fe}_2\\text{O}_3$) मुख्य अशुद्धि होती है तो किस प्रक्रिया का उपयोग किया जाता है?
o: Silica impurity: Baeyer's Process; Iron oxide impurity: Serpek's Process.
Silica impurity: Serpek's Process (White Bauxite); Iron oxide impurity: Baeyer's or Hall's Process (Red Bauxite).
Silica impurity: Hoope's Process; Iron oxide impurity: Electrolytic reduction.
Silica impurity: Carbon reduction; Iron oxide impurity: Mond's Process.
e: Explanation: Option 0 reverses the specific metallurgical purification assignments. Option 1 is correct because red bauxite containing **Iron Oxide ($\\text{Fe}_2\\text{O}_3$)** as its dominant impurity is concentrated via **Baeyer's Process** (leaching with concentrated $\\text{NaOH}$ solution) or **Hall's Process** (fusion with $\\text{Na}_2\\text{CO}_3$). Conversely, white bauxite containing **Silica ($\\text{SiO}_2$)** as its main impurity is processed via **Serpek's Process**, where the ore is heated with coke in a stream of nitrogen gas at $1800^\\circ\\text{C}$ to convert alumina into aluminium nitride ($\\text{AlN}$), separating it from volatile silicon. Option 2 lists Hoope's electrolytic refining process (used for refining crude metal, not crude ore concentration), and Option 3 lists nickel refining.

qe:
During the electrolytic reduction of purified alumina ($
\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) in the Hall-Héroult process, Cryolite ($
\text{Na}_3\text{AlF}_6$) and Fluorspar ($
\text{CaF}_2$) are added to the molten cell mixture. What dual chemical function do these additives serve?
qh: हॉल-हेरॉल्ट प्रक्रिया में शुद्ध एल्यूमिना ($\\text{Al}_2\\text{O}_3$) के इलेक्ट्रोलाइटिक अपचयन के दौरान, पिघले हुए सेल मिश्रण में क्रायोलाइट ($\\text{Na}_3\\text{AlF}_6$) और फ्लोरास्पार ($\\text{CaF}_2$) मिलाया जाता है। ये योजक कौन सा दोहरा रासायनिक कार्य करते हैं?
o: They act as oxidizing agents to convert silica into volatile gases.
They lower the melting point of alumina (from $\\sim 2050^\\circ\\text{C}$ to $\\sim 950^\\circ\\text{C}$) and increase the electrical conductivity of the molten bath.
They prevent the liberation of carbon dioxide at the graphite anode.
They precipitate elemental iron as an insoluble sludge at the cathode.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies fluoride salts as oxidizing agents. Option 1 is correct because pure Alumina ($\\text{Al}_2\\text{O}_3$) has an extremely high melting point ($\\sim 2050^\\circ\\text{C}$) and is a poor conductor of electricity in the solid/pure molten state. Adding **Cryolite ($\\text{Na}_3\\text{AlF}_6$)** and **Fluorspar ($\\text{CaF}_2$)** acts as a **Fluxing Agent** [chemical additives used to lower fusion temperatures and improve ionic mobility in melts]. This mixture lowers the melting point of the electrolyte bath down to approximately $950^\\circ\\text{C}$ and provides free $\\text{Na}^+$, $\\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\\text{Al}^{3+}$, and $\\text{F}^-$ ions to drastically increase electrical conductivity. Option 2 and Option 3 describe anode reactions or iron precipitation, which are not the roles of cryolite.

qe: Metallic aluminium reacts differently depending on the concentration and nature of the acid or alkali used. Which gas is evolved when aluminium reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid versus when it reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
qh: धात्विक एल्यूमीनियम उपयोग किए गए अम्ल या क्षार की सांद्रता और प्रकृति के आधार पर अलग-अलग प्रतिक्रिया करता है। जब एल्यूमीनियम सांद्र सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करता है बनाम जब यह जलीय सोडियम हाइड्रोक्साइड के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करता है, तो कौन सी गैस मुक्त होती है?
o: With conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$: Hydrogen gas ($\\text{H}_2$); With $\\text{NaOH}$: Oxygen gas ($\\text{O}_2$).
With conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$: Sulfur dioxide gas ($\\text{SO}_2$); With $\\text{NaOH}$: Hydrogen gas ($\\text{H}_2$).
With conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$: Hydrogen sulfide gas ($\\text{H}_2\\text{S}$); With $\\text{NaOH}$: Ammonia gas ($\\text{NH}_3$).
With conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$: Carbon monoxide; With $\\text{NaOH}$: Nitrogen dioxide.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly pairs hydrogen evolution with hot concentrated sulfuric acid. Option 1 is correct because while aluminium reacts with dilute $\\text{H}_2\\text{SO}_4$ or $\\text{HCl}$ via simple displacement to release hydrogen gas, hot **Concentrated Sulfuric Acid ($\\text{H}_2\\text{SO}_4$)** acts as an oxidizing agent. It oxidizes aluminium to aluminium sulphate while being reduced itself to release **Sulfur Dioxide Gas ($\\text{SO}_2$)**: $2\\text{Al} + 6\\text{H}_2\\text{SO}_4 \\rightarrow \\text{Al}_2(\\text{SO}_4)_3 + 3\\text{SO}_2\\uparrow + 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. When treated with strong alkalis like **Sodium Hydroxide ($\\text{NaOH}$)**, amphoteric aluminium dissolves to form sodium aluminate ($\\text{NaAlO}_2$) and liberates **Hydrogen Gas ($\\text{H}_2$)**: $2\\text{Al} + 2\\text{NaOH} + 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\rightarrow 2\\text{NaAlO}_2 + 3\\text{H}_2\\uparrow$. Option 2 and Option 3 list incorrect sulfide or ammonia gases.

qe: Lightweight aluminium alloys are engineered for specific mechanical uses. Which option correctly pairs the alloy name with its precise elemental composition and primary application?
qh: हल्के एल्यूमीनियम मिश्र धातुओं को विशिष्ट यांत्रिक उपयोगों के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। कौन सा विकल्प मिश्र धातु के नाम को उसकी सटीक तात्विक संरचना और प्राथमिक अनुप्रयोग के साथ सही ढंग से मिलाता है?
o: Duralumin: $\\text{Al}\\ (10\\%), \\text{Cu}\\ (90\\%)$; used in making heavy coins and utensils.
Duralumin: $\\text{Al}\\ (95\\%), \\text{Cu}\\ (4\\%), \\text{Mg}\\ (0.5\\%), \\text{Mn}\\ (0.5\\%)$; used in aircraft structures and pressure cookers.
Magnalium: $\\text{Al}\\ (10\\%), \\text{Ni}\\ (90\\%)$; used in nuclear fuel rods.
Aluminium Bronze: $\\text{Al}\\ (95\\%), \\text{Fe}\\ (5\\%)$; used in surgical bone pins.
e: Explanation: Option 0 confuses Duralumin with Aluminium Bronze ($\\text{Al}\\ 10\\%, \\text{Cu}\\ 90\\%$). Option 1 is correct because **Duralumin** is a high-strength, age-hardenable aluminium alloy containing **95% Aluminium ($\\text{Al}$), 4% Copper ($\\text{Cu}$), 0.5% Magnesium ($\\text{Mg}$), and 0.5% Manganese ($\\text{Mn}$)**. Adding copper, magnesium, and manganese increases its tensile strength and hardness while maintaining low density, making it ideal for aircraft airframes, automotive parts, and household pressure cookers. Magnalium contains $95-96\\% \\text{ Al}$ and $2-3\\% \\text{ Mg}$. Option 2 and Option 3 scramble alloy compositions.

qe:
Anhydrous Aluminium Chloride ($
\text{AlCl}_3$) fumes in moist air and acts as a versatile industrial chemical. What is its chemical behavior in moist air, and what reaction relies on it as a catalyst?
qh: निर्जल एल्यूमीनियम क्लोराइड ($\\text{AlCl}_3$) नम हवा में धुआँ देता है और एक बहुमुखिया औद्योगिक रसायन के रूप में कार्य करता है। नम हवा में इसका रासायनिक व्यवहार क्या है, और कौन सी प्रतिक्रिया उत्प्रेरक के रूप में इस पर निर्भर करती है?
o: It absorbs moisture without reacting; used as a catalyst in Haber's ammonia process.
It undergoes hydrolysis with moisture to release hydrogen chloride ($\\text{HCl}$) gas fumes; used as a Lewis acid catalyst in Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation reactions.
It oxidizes water into ozone gas; used as a catalyst in Ostwald's nitric acid process.
It turns into red liquor; used as a explosive propellant in rocketry.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly states it does not react with air moisture. Option 1 is correct because **Anhydrous Aluminium Chloride ($\\text{AlCl}_3$)** is an electron-deficient **Lewis Acid** [a chemical species that accepts an electron pair]. In moist air, it undergoes rapid **Hydrolysis** [a chemical breakdown reaction involving water], releasing white fumes of hydrogen chloride gas ($\\text{HCl}$): $\\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\rightarrow \\text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\\text{HCl}\\uparrow$. Because of its vacant $p$-orbitals, it acts as a catalyst in gasoline production, synthetic rubber polymerization, antiperspirants, and as a classic catalyst in **Friedel-Crafts Reactions** (alkylation and acylation of aromatic rings). Option 2 and Option 3 describe unrelated catalytic processes.

qe:
Aluminium carbide ($
\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$) is structurally classified as a 'methanide'. What gas is liberated when aluminium carbide is treated with water?
qh: एल्यूमीनियम कार्बाइड ($\\text{Al}_4\\text{C}_3$) को संरचनात्मक रूप से 'मीथेनाइड' के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया है। जब एल्यूमीनियम कार्बाइड को पानी के साथ उपचारित किया जाता है तो कौन सी गैस मुक्त होती है?
o: Acetylene gas ($\\text{C}_2\\text{H}_2$)
Methane gas ($\\text{CH}_4$)
Ethylene gas ($\\text{C}_2\\text{H}_4$)
Carbon dioxide gas ($\\text{CO}_2$)
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes the gas liberated by calcium carbide ($\\text{CaC}_2 + 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\rightarrow \\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \\text{C}_2\\text{H}_2\\uparrow$). Option 1 is correct because **Aluminium Carbide ($\\text{Al}_4\\text{C}_3$)** contains discrete $\\text{C}^{4-}$ methanide ions within its ionic crystal lattice. When treated with water or dilute acids, it undergoes complete hydrolysis to produce aluminium hydroxide and liberate **Methane Gas ($\\text{CH}_4$)**: $\\text{Al}_4\\text{C}_3 + 12\\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\rightarrow 4\\text{Al(OH)}_3 + 3\\text{CH}_4\\uparrow$. This property distinguishes methanides from acetylides (like $\\text{CaC}_2$) or allylides. Option 2 and Option 3 list incorrect hydrocarbons.

qe:
Potassium Permanganate ($
\text{KMnO}_4$) is commercially known as 'red medicine'. What chemical change occurs when solid $
\text{KMnO}_4$ crystals are heated to $200^\circ
\text{C}$?
qh: पोटेशियम परमैंगनेट ($\\text{KMnO}_4$) को व्यावसायिक रूप से 'लाल दवा' के रूप में जाना जाता है। जब ठोस $\\text{KMnO}_4$ क्रिस्टल को $200^\\circ\\text{C}$ पर गर्म किया जाता है तो कौन सा रासायनिक परिवर्तन होता है?
o: It sublimes into volatile purple vapors without releasing any gas.
It thermal-decomposes into potassium manganate ($\\text{K}_2\\text{MnO}_4$), manganese dioxide ($\\text{MnO}_2$), and oxygen gas ($\\text{O}_2$).
It reduces into metallic manganese powder and nitrogen dioxide.
It absorbs ambient water to transform into green vitriol crystals.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly proposes physical sublimation. Option 1 is correct because **Potassium Permanganate ($\\text{KMnO}_4$)** is a dark violet crystalline compound. When heated to around $200^\\circ\\text{C}$ ($473\\text{ K}$), it undergoes **Thermal Decomposition**, releasing elemental **Oxygen Gas ($\\text{O}_2$)** and converting from dark purple permanganate ($+7$ oxidation state) into green potassium manganate ($\\text{K}_2\\text{MnO}_4$, $+6$ state) and brown manganese dioxide ($\\text{MnO}_2$, $+4$ state): $2\\text{KMnO}_4 \\xrightarrow{\\Delta 200^\\circ\\text{C}} \\text{K}_2\\text{MnO}_4 + \\text{MnO}_2 + \\text{O}_2\\uparrow$. This reaction serves as a laboratory preparation method for oxygen. Option 2 and Option 3 describe incorrect reduction or hydration paths.

qe:
Iron is extracted from Haematite ($
\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$) in a blast furnace using carbon reduction. What are the distinct carbon content ranges that differentiate Pig Iron, Cast Iron, and Wrought Iron?
qh: लोहे का निष्कर्षण ब्लास्ट फर्नेस में कार्बन अपचयन का उपयोग करके हेमेटाइट ($\\text{Fe}_2\\text{O}_3$) से किया जाता है। पिग आयरन, कास्ट आयरन और गढ़ा लोहा (Wrought Iron) को अलग करने वाली विशिष्ट कार्बन सामग्री सीमाएँ क्या हैं?
o: Pig Iron: $0.1\\%$; Cast Iron: $10\\%$; Wrought Iron: $50\\%$.
Pig Iron: $\\sim 4\\%$ Carbon; Cast Iron: $\\sim 3\\%$ Carbon; Wrought Iron: $0.12\text{--}0.25\\%$ Carbon (purest commercial iron).
Pig Iron: $0.01\\%$; Cast Iron: $0.05\\%$; Wrought Iron: $4.0\\%$.
Pig Iron, Cast Iron, and Wrought Iron all contain identical carbon concentrations of $1.5\\%$.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misorders and drastically overstates carbon levels. Option 1 is correct because the commercial varieties of iron are classified by their **Carbon Content**: (1) **Pig Iron** is the crude product directly tapped from a blast furnace, containing about **$4\%$ Carbon** along with impurities ($\\text{S, P, Si, Mn}$); (2) **Cast Iron** is made by melting pig iron with scrap iron and coke, containing about **$3\%$ Carbon**, making it hard and brittle; (3) **Wrought Iron** is manufactured by oxidizing impurities from cast iron in a reverberatory furnace lined with haematite, producing the **purest commercial form of iron** with **$0.12\text{--}0.25\%$ Carbon**, making it tough, malleable, and ductile. Option 2 reverses pure and impure forms.

qe:
Iron reacts differently depending on the concentration and temperature of Nitric Acid ($
\text{HNO}_3$). What chemical phenomenon occurs when iron is treated with cold, highly concentrated $
\text{HNO}_3$?
qh: नाइट्रिक अम्ल ($\\text{HNO}_3$) की सांद्रता और तापमान के आधार पर लोहा अलग तरह से प्रतिक्रिया करता है। जब लोहे को ठंडे, अत्यधिक सांद्र $\\text{HNO}_3$ के साथ उपचारित किया जाता है तो कौन सी रासायनिक घटना घटित होती है?
o: Iron dissolves violently, evolving flammable hydrogen gas.
Iron forms a protective surface oxide layer ($\\text{Fe}_3\\text{O}_4$) that renders the metal chemically passive (unreactive).
Iron converts completely into soluble ferrous sulphate crystals.
Iron undergoes immediate meiotic cell division into nickel.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes the reaction of active metals with dilute acids, not concentrated nitric acid. Option 1 is correct because cold, highly concentrated **Nitric Acid ($\\text{HNO}_3$)** is a powerful oxidizing agent. Upon contact, it oxidizes the iron surface to form a thin, continuous, insoluble film of **Ferrosoferric Oxide ($\\text{Fe}_3\\text{O}_4$)**. This oxide layer passivates the metal, halting further reaction (**Passivity of Iron**). Passive iron will not react with dilute acids unless the protective oxide film is mechanically removed or reduced by heating in a stream of hydrogen gas ($\\text{H}_2$). Option 2 lists iron sulphate, and Option 3 introduces a biological cell division distractor.

qe: In pathological biochemistry, chronic environmental or dietary iron imbalances cause specific human diseases. What medical conditions result from iron deficiency versus excessive iron intake (as observed in African tribal populations using iron brewing vessels)?
qh: पैथोलॉजिकल बायोकेमिस्ट्री में, पुरानी पर्यावरणीय या आहार संबंधी लोहे का असंतुलन विशिष्ट मानव बीमारियों का कारण बनता है। लोहे की कमी बनाम अत्यधिक लोहे के सेवन से कौन सी चिकित्सा स्थितियां उत्पन्न होती हैं (जैसा कि लोहे के काढ़े के बर्तनों का उपयोग करने वाली अफ्रीकी जनजातीय आबादी में देखा जाता है)?
o: Deficiency: Siderosis; Excess: Anaemia.
Deficiency: Anaemia (hemoglobin deficit); Excess: Siderosis (iron overload deposit in tissues).
Deficiency: Goitre; Excess: Fluorosis.
Deficiency: Rickets; Excess: Minamata disease.
e: Explanation: Option 0 reverses the pathological deficiency and toxicity syndromes. Option 1 is correct because **Iron ($\\text{Fe}$)** is a structural component of hemoglobin in red blood cells. A **Deficiency of Iron** leads to **Anaemia** [a condition characterized by low red blood cell count or reduced hemoglobin concentration, impairing oxygen transport]. Conversely, **Excessive Intake of Iron** leads to **Siderosis** [a tissue overload disorder where excess iron deposits build up in internal organs like the liver]. A classic medical example is 'Bantu siderosis', observed in African tribal populations who brew traditional beer in unlined iron pots, leading to massive dietary iron absorption. Option 2 lists iodine/fluorine conditions, and Option 3 lists calcium/mercury conditions.

qe:
Alloy steels are fabricated by adding specific transition metals to iron to impart specialized physical properties. Which alloy steel contains 36% Nickel ($
\text{Ni}$) and exhibits almost zero thermal expansion, making it useful for clock pendulums and precision measuring tapes?
qh: विशिष्ट भौतिक गुणों को प्रदान करने के लिए लोहे में विशिष्ट संक्रमण धातुओं को जोड़कर मिश्र धातु स्टील्स (Alloy steels) बनाए जाते हैं। किस मिश्र धातु स्टील में 36% निकेल ($\\text{Ni}$) होता है और यह लगभग शून्य तापीय प्रसार (thermal expansion) प्रदर्शित करता है, जिससे यह घड़ी के पेंडुलम और सटीक मापने वाले टेप के लिए उपयोगी बनता है?
