o: Stainless Steel
Invar
Manganese Steel
Tungsten Steel
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists stainless steel ($\\text{Cr } 12\text{--}18\\%$), which is corrosion-resistant rather than zero-expansion. Option 1 is correct because **Invar** is a specialized iron-nickel alloy steel containing **36% Nickel ($\\text{Ni}$)** and about $64\%$ Iron. Its name derives from 'invariable' because it possesses an extraordinarily low Coefficient of Thermal Expansion [the fractional change in size per degree change in temperature] near ambient temperatures. This dimensional stability under thermal fluctuation makes Invar the standard material for manufacturing clock pendulums, precision measuring tapes, yardsticks, and surveying instruments. Option 2 (Manganese steel, $12-15\\% \\text{ Mn}$) is used for rock cutters, and Option 3 (Tungsten steel, $14-20\\% \\text{ W}$) is used for high-speed cutting tools.

qe:
Manganese Steel contains 12% to 15% Manganese ($
\text{Mn}$). What unique physical properties does this high manganese concentration impart to the steel alloy, and what are its primary industrial uses?
qh: मैंगनीज स्टील में 12% से 15% मैंगनीज ($\\text{Mn}$) होता है। यह उच्च मैंगनीज सांद्रता स्टील मिश्र धातु को कौन से अद्वितीय भौतिक गुण प्रदान करती है, और इसके प्राथमिक औद्योगिक उपयोग क्या हैं?
o: Makes it soft and liquid; used in surgical bone sutures.
Makes it extremely hard, resistant to wear/impact, and rust-free; used in rock crushers, burglarproof safes, and railway track frogs.
Makes it highly transparent; used in optical telescope lenses.
Makes it radioactively volatile; used as nuclear fuel cladding.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes a soft or liquid material, which contradicts the extreme hardness of manganese steel. Option 1 is correct because adding **12% to 15% Manganese ($\\text{Mn}$)** to steel produces **Hadfield Manganese Steel**. This alloy possesses high impact toughness, work-hardening capability, extreme resistance to mechanical abrasion, and rust resistance. Under heavy mechanical impact, its crystal surface hardens further. These properties make it useful for constructing heavy-duty industrial rock crushers, burglarproof bank safes, railway switches/crossing frogs, and excavator bucket teeth. Option 2 and Option 3 present optical lens or nuclear fuel distractors.

qe: Culinary cooking pans fabricated from stainless steel are often manufactured with a copper bottom layer. What thermal property justifies this bimetallic design?
qh: स्टेनलेस स्टील से बने खाना पकाने के बर्तन (cooking pans) अक्सर तांबे की निचली परत (copper bottom) के साथ निर्मित होते हैं। कौन सा तापीय गुण इस द्वि-धात्विक डिज़ाइन को सही ठहराता है?
o: Stainless steel is an electrical insulator, whereas copper is magnetic.
Copper possesses significantly higher thermal conductivity than stainless steel, ensuring rapid and uniform heat distribution across the pan base.
Copper prevents stainless steel from absorbing organic food oils.
Copper lowers the melting point of the pan to $100^\circ\text{C}$.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly calls stainless steel an electrical insulator. Option 1 is correct because while Stainless Steel ($\\text{Fe-Cr-Ni}$ alloy) is durable, strong, and corrosion-resistant, it has a relatively low **Thermal Conductivity** [the rate at which heat passes through a material, $\\sim 15\\text{ W/m}\\cdot\\text{K}$]. This low conductivity can cause localized hot spots that scorch food. **Copper ($\\text{Cu}$)** has a much higher thermal conductivity ($\\sim 400\\text{ W/m}\\cdot\\text{K}$). Bonding a copper layer to the bottom of a stainless steel pan allows heat from the burner to spread rapidly and evenly across the base before conducting into the food. Option 2 and Option 3 describe incorrect oil absorption or pan melting claims.

qe: Heat treatment of steel modifies its internal mechanical properties like hardness and elasticity through controlled heating and cooling cycles. Which choice correctly defines 'Quenching' and the resulting mechanical state of the treated steel?
qh: स्टील का उष्मा उपचार (Heat treatment) नियंत्रित हीटिंग और कूलिंग चक्रों के माध्यम से इसकी कठोरता और लोच जैसे आंतरिक यांत्रिक गुणों को संशोधित करता है। कौन सा विकल्प 'क्वेचिंग' (Quenching) और उपचारित स्टील की परिणामी यांत्रिक अवस्था को सही ढंग से परिभाषित करता है?
o: Heating steel to bright redness and cooling it very slowly; makes steel soft and ductile (Annealing).
Heating steel to bright redness and plunging it suddenly into cold water or oil; makes steel extremely hard and brittle.
Heating quenched steel to a moderate temperature below redness and cooling slowly; makes steel tough and resilient (Tempering).
Heating steel in dry ammonia gas at $500^\circ\text{C}$; forms a surface nitride coating (Nitriding).
e: Explanation: Option 0 defines Annealing (slow cooling to induce softness). Option 1 is correct because **Quenching** is a heat treatment process where steel is heated to an austenitic red-hot temperature ($\\sim 800-900^\\circ\\text{C}$) and then **rapidly cooled (quenched)** by plunging it into cold water or oil. This rapid cooling traps carbon atoms inside the iron crystal lattice, transforming the microstructure into **Martensite** [a supersaturated, highly strained tetragonal crystalline phase of iron]. This makes the quenched steel **extremely hard and brittle**. Option 2 defines Tempering (relieving brittleness), and Option 3 defines Nitriding (surface chemical treatment).

qe:
Surface treatment techniques enhance the outer wear-resistance of steel components while preserving a tough inner core. What process involves heating steel in an atmosphere of dry ammonia gas at $500
--600^\circ
\text{C}$ for several days, and what protective surface layer forms?
qh: सतह उपचार तकनीकें (Surface treatment techniques) एक कठिन आंतरिक कोर को संरक्षित करते हुए स्टील घटकों के बाहरी पहनने के प्रतिरोध को बढ़ाती हैं। किस प्रक्रिया में शुष्क अमोनिया गैस के वातावरण में $500--600^\circ\text{C}$ पर कई दिनों तक स्टील को गर्म करना शामिल है, और कौन सी सुरक्षात्मक सतह परत बनती है?
o: Case Hardening; forms a surface layer of iron oxide.
Nitriding; forms an extremely hard protective surface coating of Iron Nitride.
Annealing; forms a flexible layer of organic suberin.
Galvanizing; forms a surface film of zinc carbonate.
e: Explanation: Option 0 names case hardening (which uses charcoal to introduce carbon) and claims an oxide forms. Option 1 is correct because **Nitriding** is a surface-hardening heat treatment where steel alloys are heated in a furnace containing **Dry Ammonia Gas ($\\text{NH}_3$)** at temperatures between $500^\circ\\text{C}$ and $600^\\circ\\text{C}$ for 3 to 4 days. The thermal dissociation of ammonia yields atomic nitrogen ($\\text{N}$), which diffuses into the outer surface layers of the steel and reacts with iron and alloying elements to form a hard, wear-resistant coating of **Iron Nitride** [and alloy nitrides]. This increases surface hardness and fatigue resistance without requiring a liquid quench. Option 2 defines bulk annealing, and Option 3 describes zinc coating.

qe:
Super Phosphate of Lime $[
\text{CaH}_4(
\text{PO}_4)_2 + 
\text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2
\text{H}_2
\text{O}]$ is an important agricultural fertilizer. Why is this mixture preferred over raw insoluble rock phosphate (phosphorite) for crop application?
qh: सुपर फास्फेट ऑफ लाइम [$ \text{CaH}_4(\text{PO}_4)_2 + \text{CaSO}_4 \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$] एक महत्वपूर्ण कृषि उर्वरक है। फसल अनुप्रयोग के लिए कच्चे अघुलनशील रॉक फॉस्फेट (फॉस्फोराइट) की तुलना में इस मिश्रण को क्यों प्राथमिकता दी जाती है?
o: Because super phosphate of lime is insoluble in water and stays in the soil for 100 years.

Because treatment with sulfuric acid converts insoluble tri-calcium phosphate into water-soluble monocalcium phosphate [$\text{CaH}_4(\text{PO}_4)_2$], making phosphate ions readily bioavailable for plant root absorption.
Because it acts as an insecticide that converts plant roots into metallic copper.
Because it lowers the soil temperature to absolute zero to freeze weed seeds.
e: Explanation: Option 0 claims water insolubility, which would prevent plant root uptake. Option 1 is correct because natural rock phosphate (phosphorite, $\\text{Ca}_3(\\text{PO}_4)_2$) is insoluble in water, meaning plant roots cannot absorb its phosphate content. Treating rock phosphate with concentrated sulfuric acid converts it into **Super Phosphate of Lime**, a mixture containing **Water-Soluble Monocalcium Phosphate [Calcium Dihydrogen Phosphate, $\\text{CaH}_4(\\text{PO}_4)_2$]** and gypsum ($\\text{CaSO}_4 \\cdot 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$). Because it is water-soluble, it dissolves in soil moisture, allowing plant roots to absorb phosphate ions ($\\text{H}_2\\text{PO}_4^-$) for ATP synthesis and crop growth. Option 2 and Option 3 describe impossible chemical transmutations or absolute zero temperatures.

qe:
Anhydrous aluminium chloride ($
\text{AlCl}_3$) fumes in moist air and acts as a hardening agent, antiperspirant, and catalyst. What is its molecular structure in the vapor phase or non-polar solvents at moderate temperatures?
qh: निर्जल एल्यूमीनियम क्लोराइड ($\\text{AlCl}_3$) नम हवा में धुआँ देता है और एक सख्त एजेंट, एंटीपर्सपिरेंट और उत्प्रेरक के रूप में कार्य करता है। मध्यम तापमान पर वाष्प चरण या गैर-ध्रुवीय विलायकों में इसकी आणविक संरचना क्या है?
o: It exists as an ionic crystal lattice composed of $\text{Al}^{3+}$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions.
It exists as a covalent dimer molecule ($\\text{Al}_2\\text{Cl}_6$) held by coordinate covalent bonds between chlorine atoms and electron-deficient aluminium centers.
It exists as a metallic liquid amalgam dissolved in mercury.
It decomposes completely into elemental aluminium powder and chlorine gas.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies vapor-phase $\\text{AlCl}_3$ as a simple ionic lattice. Option 1 is correct because an isolated monomeric $\\text{AlCl}_3$ molecule has only 6 valence electrons around the central aluminium atom, making it an electron-deficient **Lewis Acid**. To achieve a stable octet, two $\\text{AlCl}_3$ molecules combine at moderate temperatures (in non-polar solvents or vapor phase below $400^\\circ\\text{C}$) to form a **Covalent Dimer ($\\text{Al}_2\\text{Cl}_6$)**. In this dimer, two chlorine atoms form bridge bonds by donating lone pairs via coordinate covalent bonds to adjacent aluminium atoms, completing their octets. At high temperatures ($>800^\\circ\\text{C}$), the dimer dissociates back into trigonal planar monomeric $\\text{AlCl}_3$. Option 2 and Option 3 describe mercury amalgams or incorrect thermal breakdown.

qe: Hydrated ferrous sulphate ($\\text{FeSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) is known as green vitriol. Which choice correctly describes its preparation into Mohr's salt, and what is its specific chemical classification?
qh: हाइड्रेटेड फेरस सल्फेट ($\\text{FeSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) को हरा कसीस (green vitriol) कहा जाता है। कौन सा विकल्प मोहर लवण (Mohr's salt) में इसके निर्माण का सही वर्णन करता है, और इसका विशिष्ट रासायनिक वर्गीकरण क्या है?
o: Mixing ferrous sulphate with copper sulphate in boiling water; classified as a complex coordination salt.

Mixing saturated solutions of ferrous sulphate and ammonium sulphate in pure air-free distilled water; classified as a double salt [$\\text{FeSO}_4 \\cdot (\\text{NH}_4)_2\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$].
Treating green vitriol with nitric acid in open air; classified as a basic oxide.
Dissolving iron in liquid ammonia; classified as an organometallic polymer.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies the second sulphate component as copper sulphate and misclassifies the product. Option 1 is correct because **Mohr's Salt** (Ferrous Ammonium Sulphate, $\\text{FeSO}_4 \\cdot (\\text{NH}_4)_2\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) is prepared by mixing equimolar saturated solutions of pure ferrous sulphate and ammonium sulphate in air-free distilled water (to prevent aerial oxidation of $\\text{Fe}^{2+}$ to $\\text{Fe}^{3+}$). It is classified as a **Double Salt** [an inorganic salt complex that contains more than one cation or anion, which completely dissociates into its constituent simple ions when dissolved in water]. Option 2 and Option 3 introduce incorrect reagents or polymer classifications.

qe: Copper ($\\text{Cu}$, $Z=29$) displays specific reaction paths when treated with nitric acid ($\\text{HNO}_3$) depending on concentration. Which option correctly matches the acid concentration with the specific nitrogen oxide gas evolved?
qh: तांबा ($\\text{Cu}$, $Z=29$) सांद्रता के आधार पर नाइट्रिक अम्ल ($\\text{HNO}_3$) के साथ उपचारित करने पर विशिष्ट प्रतिक्रिया पथ प्रदर्शित करता है। कौन सा विकल्प अम्ल की सांद्रता को निकलने वाली विशिष्ट नाइट्रोजन ऑक्साइड गैस के साथ सही ढंग से मिलाता है?
o: Dilute $\\text{HNO}_3$: $\\text{NO}_2$ gas; $50\%$ $\\text{HNO}_3$: $\\text{N}_2\\text{O}$ gas; Concentrated $\\text{HNO}_3$: $\\text{NO}$ gas.
Dilute $\\text{HNO}_3$: Nitrous oxide ($\\text{N}_2\\text{O}$); $50\%$ $\\text{HNO}_3$: Nitric oxide ($\\text{NO}$); Concentrated $\\text{HNO}_3$: Nitrogen dioxide ($\\text{NO}_2$).
Dilute $\\text{HNO}_3$: Ammonia gas; $50\%$ $\\text{HNO}_3$: Oxygen gas; Concentrated $\\text{HNO}_3$: Hydrogen gas.
All concentrations of $\\text{HNO}_3$ liberate pure $\\text{H}_2$ gas exclusively.
e: Explanation: Option 0 completely scrambles the nitrogen oxide product assignments across concentrations. Option 1 is correct because copper is an unreactive metal below hydrogen in the activity series, meaning it does not liberate $\\text{H}_2$ with acids; instead, it reduces nitric acid via distinct **Oxidative Cleavage** paths depending on concentration: (1) **Dilute $\\text{HNO}_3$** yields **Nitrous Oxide ($\\text{N}_2\\text{O}$)** gas; (2) **$50\%$ $\\text{HNO}_3$** yields **Nitric Oxide ($\\text{NO}$)** gas; and (3) **Hot Concentrated $\\text{HNO}_3$** yields dense brown **Nitrogen Dioxide ($\\text{NO}_2$)** gas. (Passing $\\text{HNO}_3$ vapors over hot copper yields $\\text{N}_2$ gas). Option 2 and Option 3 describe impossible hydrogen or oxygen gas paths.

qe: Specialized copper alloys are engineered for marine, electrical, and decorative uses. Which option correctly matches the alloy name with its specific composition and unique industrial application?
qh: विशिष्ट तांबा मिश्र धातुओं (copper alloys) को समुद्री, विद्युत और सजावटी उपयोगों के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। कौन सा विकल्प मिश्र धातु के नाम को उसकी विशिष्ट संरचना और अद्वितीय औद्योगिक अनुप्रयोग के साथ सही ढंग से मिलाता है?
o: German Silver: $\\text{Cu}\\ (50\\%), \\text{Ag}\\ (50\\%)$; used in silver coins.
Delta Metal: $\\text{Cu}\\ (60\\%), \\text{Zn}\\ (38\\%), \\text{Fe}\\ (2\\%)$; highly resistant to sea water, used in ship propellers.
Rolled Gold: $\\text{Cu}\\ (10\\%), \\text{Au}\\ (90\\%)$; used in high-grade bullion reserves.
Monel Metal: $\\text{Cu}\\ (10\\%), \\text{Sn}\\ (90\\%)$; used in acid-sensitive glass filters.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly states German Silver contains elemental silver (German Silver contains $\\text{Cu}\\ 50\\%, \\text{Zn}\\ 35\\%, \\text{Ni}\\ 15\\%$ and zero silver). Option 1 is correct because **Delta Metal** is a high-tensile copper alloy containing **$60\%$ Copper ($\\text{Cu}$), $38\%$ Zinc ($\\text{Zn}$), and $2\%$ Iron ($\\text{Fe}$)**. Incorporating iron increases its mechanical toughness and renders it exceptionally resistant to corrosion by salt water, making it ideal for casting marine ship propellers. Option 2 confuses Rolled Gold ($\\text{Cu}\\ 90\\%, \\text{Al}\\ 10\\%$) with real gold, and Option 3 misidentifies Monel Metal ($\\text{Cu}\\ 70\\%, \\text{Ni}\\ 30\\%$).

qe: Fehling's solution is a standard analytical reagent used to detect reducing sugars and aldehydes. What are the two distinct chemical components that constitute Fehling's Solution A and Fehling's Solution B?
qh: फेलिंग घोल (Fehling's solution) एक मानक विश्लेषणात्मक अभिकर्मक है जिसका उपयोग अपचायी शर्करा (reducing sugars) और एल्डिहाइड का पता लगाने के लिए किया जाता है। फेलिंग घोल A और फेलिंग घोल B बनाने वाले दो विशिष्ट रासायनिक घटक क्या हैं?
o: Fehling A: Ferrous sulphate; Fehling B: Concentrated nitric acid.
Fehling A: Aqueous Copper Sulphate ($\\text{CuSO}_4$); Fehling B: Alkaline solution of Sodium Potassium Tartrate (Rochelle Salt).
Fehling A: Silver nitrate; Fehling B: Ammonium hydroxide.
Fehling A: Zinc sulphate; Fehling B: Barium sulphide.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies Fehling A as an iron salt. Option 1 is correct because **Fehling's Solution** is prepared by mixing two separate solutions prior to testing: **Fehling Solution A** is an aqueous solution of **Copper(II) Sulphate ($\\text{CuSO}_4$)**, and **Fehling Solution B** is a strongly alkaline solution of **Sodium Potassium Tartrate (Rochelle Salt, $\\text{KNaC}_4\\text{H}_4\\text{O}_6 \\cdot 4\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$)** dissolved in $\\text{NaOH}$. When heated with aldehydes or monosaccharides (like glucose), $\\text{Cu}^{2+}$ is reduced to form a characteristic brick-red precipitate of **Copper(I) Oxide ($\\text{Cu}_2\\text{O}$)**. Option 2 describes Tollen's reagent, and Option 3 describes lithopone reagents.

qe: Eating boiled eggs with a solid silver spoon causes the silver surface to tarnish rapidly. What chemical compound forms on the spoon, and what component in the egg causes this reaction?
qh: ठोस चांदी के चम्मच से उबले अंडे खाने से चांदी की सतह तेजी से बदरंग (tarnish) हो जाती है। चम्मच पर कौन सा रासायनिक यौगिक बनता है, और अंडे में कौन सा घटक इस प्रतिक्रिया का कारण बनता है?
o: Silver chloride ($\\text{AgCl}$); caused by sodium chloride in egg white.
Silver sulphide ($\\text{Ag}_2\\text{S}$); caused by sulfur contained in egg proteins reacting with silver metal to form a black surface layer.
Silver oxide ($\\text{Ag}_2\\text{O}$); caused by dissolved oxygen inside the yolk.
Sodium argento cyanide; caused by organic cyanides in albumen.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies the tarnish as silver chloride. Option 1 is correct because egg proteins (like ovalbumin) are rich in sulfur-containing amino acids (cysteine and methionine). When eating eggs, sulfur compounds break down and react readily with metallic silver ($\\text{Ag}$) to form a thin, tightly adherent, black surface coating of **Silver Sulphide ($\\text{Ag}_2\\text{S}$)**: $2\\text{Ag} + \\text{S} \\rightarrow \\text{Ag}_2\\text{S}$. This chemical tarnish damages and discolors silver cutlery. Option 2 and Option 3 describe incorrect oxide or complex cyanide pathways.

qe: Silver halides display light sensitivity and are applied across specialized photographic and meteorological fields. Which choice correctly coordinates Silver Bromide, Silver Chloride, and Silver Iodide with their primary applications?
qh: सिल्वर हैलाइड (Silver halides) प्रकाश के प्रति संवेदनशीलता प्रदर्शित करते हैं और विशेष फोटोग्राफिक तथा मौसम संबंधी क्षेत्रों में लागू होते हैं। कौन सा विकल्प सिल्वर ब्रोमाइड, सिल्वर क्लोराइड और सिल्वर आयोडाइड को उनके प्राथमिक अनुप्रयोगों के साथ सही ढंग से मिलाता है?
o: $\\text{AgBr}$: Artificial rain; $\\text{AgCl}$: Black-and-white photography; $\\text{AgI}$: Photochromatic glasses.
$\\text{AgBr}$: Photography; $\\text{AgCl}$: Photochromatic glasses; $\\text{AgI}$: Cloud seeding to produce artificial rain.
$\\text{AgBr}$: Dental cavity filling; $\\text{AgCl}$: Water purification; $\\text{AgI}$: Anti-scaling agent.
$\\text{AgBr}$: Hair dye; $\\text{AgCl}$: Anti-chlor agent; $\\text{AgI}$: Electroplating bath.
e: Explanation: Option 0 scrambles the specific practical uses of the halides. Option 1 is correct because: (1) **Silver Bromide ($\\text{AgBr}$)** undergoes light-induced reduction to metallic silver, making it the light-sensitive agent in traditional **Photographic Emulsions**; (2) **Silver Chloride ($\\text{AgCl}$)** undergoes reversible photo-reduction, making it the active ingredient in **Photochromatic Glasses** that darken in sunlight; and (3) **Silver Iodide ($\\text{AgI}$)** has a crystal structure closely matching ice, making it an effective nucleating agent in **Cloud Seeding for Artificial Rain**. Option 2 and Option 3 list incorrect medical or metallurgical uses.

qe:
Silver Nitrate ($
\text{AgNO}_3$), commonly known as Lunar Caustic, is stored in dark brown glass bottles. Why is dark storage required, and what is its application in democratic electoral processes?
qh: सिल्वर नाइट्रेट ($\\text{AgNO}_3$), जिसे आमतौर पर लूनर कॉस्टिक (Lunar Caustic) कहा जाता है, को गहरे भूरे रंग की कांच की बोतलों में संग्रहीत किया जाता है। अंधेरे भंडारण की आवश्यकता क्यों है, और लोकतांत्रिक चुनावी प्रक्रियाओं में इसका क्या उपयोग है?
o: Stored in dark bottles to absorb oxygen gas; used as a liquid electrolyte in lead-acid batteries.
Stored in dark bottles because sunlight decomposes it into metallic silver; used as an indelible voter marking ink applied to voters' fingers.
Stored in dark bottles to prevent vaporization; used as a oral antacid to neutralize stomach $\\text{HCl}$.
Stored in dark bottles to absorb atmospheric nitrogen; used to weld railway tracks.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies its storage mechanics and assigns lead-acid battery functions to silver nitrate. Option 1 is correct because **Silver Nitrate ($\\text{AgNO}_3$, Lunar Caustic)** is photochemically unstable. When exposed to ambient sunlight or UV radiation, it undergoes **Photolytic Decomposition**, breaking down into black metallic silver, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen: $2\\text{AgNO}_3 \\xrightarrow{h\\nu} 2\\text{Ag} + 2\\text{NO}_2\\uparrow + \\text{O}_2\\uparrow$. Storing it in dark brown bottles blocks light wavelengths to prevent this decomposition. In elections, $\\text{AgNO}_3$ is used in **Indelible Voter Ink**; upon skin contact, it reacts with skin salt and protein to form insoluble $\\text{AgCl}$ and metallic silver stains that cannot be washed off. Option 2 and Option 3 describe antacid or thermit welding processes.

qe: Gold ($Z=79$) is an unreactive noble metal that resists most concentrated mineral acids. What reagent mixture dissolves pure gold, and what chemical complex forms during dissolution?
qh: सोना ($Z=79$) एक अप्रतिक्रियाशील नोबल धातु है जो अधिकांश सांद्र खनिज अम्लों का विरोध करता है। कौन सा अभिकर्मक मिश्रण (reagent mixture) शुद्ध सोने को घोलता है, और घुलने के दौरान कौन सा रासायनिक कॉम्प्लेक्स बनता है?
o: Concentrated sulfuric acid alone; yields gold sulphate salt.
Aqua-regia (fresh mixture of conc. $\\text{HCl}$ and conc. $\\text{HNO}_3$ in 3:1 ratio); dissolves gold by forming soluble tetrachloroauric(III) acid [$\\text{HAuCl}_4$].
Boiling sodium hydroxide solution; yields solid gold hydroxide precipitate.
Liquid ammonia at $200^\\circ\\text{C}$; yields gold amide crystals.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly claims sulfuric acid alone can dissolve gold. Option 1 is correct because gold is a noble metal that does not react with single mineral acids. It dissolves in **Aqua-Regia** [a freshly prepared, highly corrosive liquid mixture composed of **3 parts concentrated Hydrochloric Acid ($\\text{HCl}$) to 1 part concentrated Nitric Acid ($\\text{HNO}_3$)**]. Nitric acid acts as a powerful oxidant, while hydrochloric acid provides chloride ions to form the soluble coordination complex **Tetrachloroauric(III) Acid ($\\text{HAuCl}_4$)**: $\\text{Au} + 3\\text{HNO}_3 + 4\\text{HCl} \\rightarrow \\text{HAuCl}_4 + 3\\text{NO}_2\\uparrow + 3\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. Option 2 and Option 3 list basic alkalis or ammonia, which do not dissolve gold.

qe: The purity of gold is expressed in 'carats'. What is the gold purity percentage of 18-carat gold, and why is copper or silver alloyed into pure 24-carat gold during jewelry manufacturing?
qh: सोने की शुद्धता को 'कैरेट' (carat) में व्यक्त किया जाता है। 18-कैरेट सोने की सोने की शुद्धता प्रतिशत क्या है, और आभूषण निर्माण के दौरान शुद्ध 24-कैरेट सोने में तांबा या चांदी क्यों मिलाया जाता है?
o: Purity: $100\\%$; Copper is added to lower the density to absolute zero.
Purity: $75\\%$; Pure 24-carat gold is too soft and malleable to retain shapes, so copper/silver is added to impart structural hardness.
Purity: $50\\%$; Copper is added to make gold magnetic.
Purity: $18\\%$; Copper is added to prevent alpha decay.
e: Explanation: Option 0 claims 18-carat is $100\%$ pure (24-carat is $100\%$ pure). Option 1 is correct because gold purity is measured on a 24-part scale where **24-carat gold represents $100\%$ pure gold**. The fractional purity of 18-carat gold is calculated as $\\frac{18}{24} = 0.75$, or **$75\%$ pure gold** (with $25\%$, or 6 parts, consisting of alloyed metals like copper or silver). Pure 24-carat gold is extremely soft and easily deforms under mechanical strain. Adding copper or silver distorts the gold crystal lattice, providing the structural **Hardness** and durability required for jewelry to hold its shape. Option 2 and Option 3 miscalculate the carat percentage.

qe: In ornamental arts and pottery coloring, a specialized preparation known as 'Purple of Cassius' is used. What is the chemical composition and nature of Purple of Cassius?
qh: आभूषण कला और मिट्टी के बर्तनों के रंग में, 'पर्पल ऑफ कासियस' (Purple of Cassius) के रूप में जाना जाने वाला एक विशेष फॉर्मूलेशन इस्तेमाल किया जाता है। पर्पल ऑफ कासियस की रासायनिक संरचना और प्रकृति क्या है?
o: A liquid solution of potassium permanganate in vinegar.
A colloidal preparation of gold absorbed on stannic hydroxide [$\\text{Au} + \\text{Sn(OH)}_4$], exhibiting a deep purple color.
A dry mixture of copper sulphate and basic copper carbonate.
A crystalline powder of silver iodide and charcoal.
e: Explanation: Option 0 confuses purple of Cassius with potassium permanganate ('red medicine'). Option 1 is correct because **Purple of Cassius** is a **Colloidal Gold** preparation formed by reacting gold(III) chloride solution with stannous chloride ($\\text{SnCl}_2$). The redox reaction precipitates finely divided metallic gold particles stabilized by absorption onto hydrated stannic hydroxide [**$\\text{Au} + \\text{Sn(OH)}_4$**]. It exhibits a distinct deep purple/ruby color and is water-immiscible, making it valuable for coloring expensive ceramics, porcelain, and manufacturing ruby glass. Option 2 and Option 3 describe copper or silver salt mixtures.

qe:
Zinc ($Z=30$) is a Group-12 transition block element. What chemical product forms when zinc metal reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide ($
\text{NaOH}$), and what gas is evolved?
qh: जिंक ($Z=30$) एक समूह-12 संक्रमण ब्लॉक तत्व है। जब जिंक धातु जलीय सोडियम हाइड्रोक्साइड ($\\text{NaOH}$) के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करती है तो कौन सा रासायनिक उत्पाद बनता है, और कौन सी गैस मुक्त होती है?
o: Forms Zinc hydroxide and liberates oxygen gas.
Forms Sodium Zincate ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{ZnO}_2$) and liberates Hydrogen gas ($\\text{H}_2$).
Forms Zinc chloride and liberates sulfur dioxide gas.
Forms Basic copper carbonate and liberates nitrogen gas.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly states oxygen gas is evolved. Option 1 is correct because zinc is an **Amphoteric Metal** [a metal capable of reacting with both strong mineral acids and strong alkalis to produce a salt and hydrogen gas]. When zinc is heated with an aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide ($\\text{NaOH}$), it dissolves to form a soluble oxoanion complex salt, **Sodium Zincate ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{ZnO}_2$)**, and liberates **Hydrogen Gas ($\\text{H}_2$)**: $\\text{Zn} + 2\\text{NaOH} \\rightarrow \\text{Na}_2\\text{ZnO}_2 + \\text{H}_2\\uparrow$. Option 2 and Option 3 list non-amphoteric acid or copper reaction products.

qe: Lithopone is a widely used white pigment in paints and enamels. What are the two chemical compounds that constitute Lithopone, and how is it synthesized?
qh: लिथोफोन (Lithopone) पेंट और इनेमल में व्यापक रूप से इस्तेमाल किया जाने वाला एक सफेद वर्णक (white pigment) है। लिथोफोन बनाने वाले दो रासायनिक यौगिक कौन से हैं, और इसका संश्लेषण कैसे किया जाता है?
o: Mixture of $\\text{TiO}_2$ and $\\text{CaCO}_3$; prepared by slaking quicklime with acid.
Co-precipitated mixture of Barium Sulphate ($\\text{BaSO}_4$) and Zinc Sulphide ($\\text{ZnS}$); prepared by reacting zinc sulphate with barium sulphide.
Mixture of $\\text{PbO}$ and $\\text{ZnO}$; prepared by heating galena with coke.
Mixture of $\\text{CuSO}_4$ and $\\text{NaCl}$; prepared by evaporating brine.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes titanium white paint mixtures. Option 1 is correct because **Lithopone** is an insoluble white pigment mixture consisting of **Barium Sulphate ($\\text{BaSO}_4$) and Zinc Sulphide ($\\text{ZnS}$)**. It is synthesized by mixing aqueous solutions of zinc sulphate ($\\text{ZnSO}_4$) and barium sulphide ($\\text{BaS}$), driving a double displacement reaction that precipitates both insoluble salts simultaneously: $\\text{ZnSO}_4(aq) + \\text{BaS}(aq) \\rightarrow \\text{ZnS}\\downarrow + \\text{BaSO}_4\\downarrow$. Unlike lead-based white paints, lithopone does not darken when exposed to atmospheric hydrogen sulfide ($\\text{H}_2\\text{S}$) gas. Option 2 lists toxic lead compounds, and Option 3 lists soluble copper/sodium salts.

qe:
The commercial white paint pigment Lithopone ($
\text{BaSO}_4 + 
\text{ZnS}$) exhibits a distinct optical behavior when exposed to sunlight versus when placed in the dark. What optical transition occurs?
qh: वाणिज्यिक सफेद पेंट वर्णक लिथोफोन ($\\text{BaSO}_4 + \\text{ZnS}$) धूप में संपर्क में आने पर बनाम अंधेरे में रखे जाने पर एक विशिष्ट ऑप्टिकल व्यवहार प्रदर्शित करता है। कौन सा ऑप्टिकल संक्रमण होता है?
o: Turns bright green in sunlight and dark red in the dark.
Turns grey in sunlight (due to light-induced reversible reduction) and reverts to white in the dark.
Turns black permanently in sunlight and dissolves into a liquid in the dark.
Emits blue laser radiation in sunlight and turns invisible in the dark.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes incorrect chromatic shifts. Option 1 is correct because **Lithopone** exhibits a unique photochemical property: upon exposure to direct UV radiation in **Sunlight**, the zinc sulphide component undergoes a reversible partial photolysis, forming microscopic traces of elemental zinc that cause the white pigment to **Turn Grey**. When returned to the **Dark**, this trace zinc re-oxidizes, and the pigment **Reverts to its original White Color**. This property is considered when formulating outdoor paints. Option 2 claims permanent blackening, and Option 3 introduces impossible laser emission claims.

qe:
Copper sulphate pentahydrate ($
\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5
\text{H}_2
\text{O}$) is known as Blue Vitriol or Nila Thotha. What agricultural fungicide formulation is prepared using copper sulphate mixed with slaked lime?
qh: कॉपर सल्फेट पेंटाहाइड्रेट ($\\text{CuSO}_4 \\cdot 5\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) को नीला थोथा (Blue Vitriol) कहा जाता है। बुझे हुए चूने के साथ मिलाकर कॉपर सल्फेट का उपयोग करके कौन सा कृषि कवकनाशी (agricultural fungicide) फॉर्मूलेशन तैयार किया जाता है?
o: Chestnut Compound
Bordeaux Mixture
Lithopone Paste
Mohr's Solution
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes Chestnut compound, which is prepared by mixing copper sulphate with ammonium carbonate ($\\text{NH}_4\\text{HCO}_3$), not slaked lime. Option 1 is correct because **Bordeaux Mixture** is a famous agricultural fungicide and germicide prepared by mixing **Copper Sulphate ($\\text{CuSO}_4$) with Slaked Lime [Calcium Hydroxide, $\\text{Ca(OH)}_2$]** in water. It is sprayed on crops, fruit trees, and grapevines to prevent fungal diseases like downy mildew and 'damping off' of seedlings. Option 2 lists paint pigments, and Option 3 lists double salts.

qe: Jeweller's rouge is a fine abrasive powder used for polishing glass, optical lenses, and precious metal jewelry. What is the chemical composition of jeweller's rouge?
qh: ज्वैलर्स रूज (Jeweller's rouge) एक सूक्ष्म अपघर्षी पाउडर (fine abrasive powder) है जिसका उपयोग कांच, ऑप्टिकल लेंस और कीमती धातु के आभूषणों को पॉलिश करने के लिए किया जाता है। ज्वैलर्स रूज की रासायनिक संरचना क्या है?
o: Ferrous oxide ($\\text{FeO}$)
Ferric oxide ($\\text{Fe}_2\\text{O}_3$)
Copper(II) oxide ($\\text{CuO}$)
Zinc oxide ($\\text{ZnO}$)
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists ferrous oxide ($+2$ oxidation state), which is a black, unstable oxide. Option 1 is correct because **Jeweller's Rouge** (also known as rouge or red iron oxide) is chemically composed of anhydrous **Ferric Oxide ($\\text{Fe}_2\\text{O}_3$)**, where iron exists in the $+3$ oxidation state. It is prepared by calcining ferrous sulphate crystals. Because of its extremely fine particle size and moderate hardness, it acts as a mild buffing and polishing agent that smooths micro-scratches on glass, gold, and silver without gouging the metal. Option 2 and Option 3 list copper or zinc oxides.

qe: Transition metals are defined by their electronic configurations. What is the ground-state valence electronic configuration of Copper ($Z=29$) and Gold ($Z=79$) in the Modern Periodic Table?
qh: संक्रमण धातुओं को उनके इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास द्वारा परिभाषित किया जाता है। आधुनिक आवर्त सारणी में कॉपर ($Z=29$) और गोल्ड ($Z=79$) का ग्राउंड-स्टेट वैलेंस इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास क्या है?
o: Copper: $[\\text{Ar}]3\\text{d}^9 4\\text{s}^2$; Gold: $[\\text{Xe}]4\\text{f}^{14} 5\\text{d}^9 6\\text{s}^2$
Copper: $[\\text{Ar}]3\\text{d}^{10} 4\\text{s}^1$; Gold: $[\\text{Xe}]4\\text{f}^{14} 5\\text{d}^{10} 6\\text{s}^1$
Copper: $[\\text{Ar}]3\\text{d}^8 4\\text{s}^3$; Gold: $[\\text{Xe}]5\\text{d}^{10} 6\\text{s}^2$
Copper: $[\\text{Ar}]4\\text{s}^2 4\\text{p}^6$; Gold: $[\\text{Xe}]6\\text{s}^1 6\\text{p}^6$
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists expected Aufbau configurations ($d^9 s^2$) that ignore half-filled/fully-filled subshell stability anomalies. Option 1 is correct because both Copper (Group 11, Period 4) and Gold (Group 11, Period 6) exhibit **Anomalous Electronic Configurations** driven by the extra thermodynamic stability of a completely filled $d^{10}$ subshell. An electron promotes from the outermost $s$-orbital to complete the $d$-subshell: **Copper ($Z=29$)** has the configuration **$[\\text{Ar}]3\\text{d}^{10} 4\\text{s}^1$**, and **Gold ($Z=79$)** has the configuration **$[\\text{Xe}]4\\text{f}^{14} 5\\text{d}^{10} 6\\text{s}^1$**. Option 2 and Option 3 present invalid orbital configurations.

qe:
Extraction of silver and gold from low-grade ores utilizes cyanide leaching processes. What soluble coordination complex forms when silver ore is dissolved in aqueous sodium cyanide ($
\text{NaCN}$) in the presence of air?
qh: निम्न श्रेणी के अयस्कों से चांदी और सोने का निष्कर्षण साइनाइड लीचिंग प्रक्रियाओं का उपयोग करता है। वायु की उपस्थिति में जलीय सोडियम साइनाइड ($\\text{NaCN}$) में चांदी के अयस्क को घोलने पर कौन सा घुलनशील समन्वय जटिल (soluble coordination complex) बनता है?
o: Sodium sulphate complex, $\\text{Na}_2\\text{SO}_4$
Sodium argentocyanide complex, $\\text{Na}[\\text{Ag}(\\text{CN})_2]$ (or dicyanoargentate(I) anion)
Silver nitrate complex, $\\text{AgNO}_3$
Sodium zincate complex, $\\text{Na}_2\\text{ZnO}_2$
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists simple sodium sulphate. Option 1 is correct because in the **MacArthur-Forrest Cyanide Process** for extracting silver or gold, argentite ore ($\\text{Ag}_2\\text{S}$) or native silver is leached with a dilute ($0.5\%$) aqueous solution of **Sodium Cyanide ($\\text{NaCN}$)** in the presence of atmospheric oxygen. Silver dissolves to form a water-soluble coordination complex, **Sodium Argentocyanide [$\\text{Na}[\\text{Ag}(\\text{CN})_2]$]**: $\\text{Ag}_2\\text{S} + 4\\text{NaCN} + 2\\text{O}_2 \\rightarrow 2\\text{Na}[\\text{Ag}(\\text{CN})_2] + \\text{Na}_2\\text{SO}_4$. Silver metal is then precipitated from this complex by adding active zinc dust ($\\text{Zn}$). Option 2 lists silver nitrate, and Option 3 lists sodium zincate.

qe:
Zinc Sulphate ($
\text{ZnSO}_4 \cdot 7
\text{H}_2
\text{O}$) forms double salts with alkali metal sulphates. What is the common name of hydrated zinc sulphate, and what chemical formula represents its double salt with potassium sulphate?
qh: जिंक सल्फेट ($\\text{ZnSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) क्षार धातु सल्फेट्स के साथ दोहरा लवण बनाता है। हाइड्रेटेड जिंक सल्फेट का सामान्य नाम क्या है, और कौन सा रासायनिक सूत्र पोटेशियम सल्फेट के साथ इसके दोहरे लवण का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है?
o: Blue Vitriol; formula: $\\text{CuSO}_4 \\cdot \\text{ZnSO}_4 \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$
White Vitriol; formula: $\\text{K}_2\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot \\text{ZnSO}_4 \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$
Green Vitriol; formula: $\\text{FeSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$
Lunar Caustic; formula: $\\text{AgNO}_3 \\cdot \\text{KNO}_3$
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies zinc sulphate as Blue Vitriol (which is copper sulphate). Option 1 is correct because hydrated zinc sulphate ($\\text{ZnSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) is commercially known as **White Vitriol**. Like other transition metal sulphates, it crystallizes with alkali metal sulphates to form double salts known as Tutton's salts, having the general formula $\\text{M}_2\\text{I}\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot \\text{M}\\text{II}\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$. Its double salt with potassium sulphate is represented as **$\\text{K}_2\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot \\text{ZnSO}_4 \\cdot 6\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$**. Option 2 identifies Green Vitriol (ferrous sulphate), and Option 3 identifies Lunar Caustic (silver nitrate).

qe: Biological systems depend on trace transition metal complexes for respiratory catalysis. Which transition metal serves as the core functional component inside the respiratory enzyme complex Cytochrome C Oxidase?
qh: जैविक प्रणालियाँ श्वसन उत्प्रेरण के लिए ट्रेस संक्रमण धातु परिसरों (trace transition metal complexes) पर निर्भर करती हैं। कौन सी संक्रमण धातु श्वसन एंजाइम परिसर सायटोक्रोम सी ऑक्सीडेज (Cytochrome C Oxidase) के अंदर कोर कार्यात्मक घटक के रूप में कार्य करती है?
o: Zinc ($\\text{Zn}$)
Copper ($\\text{Cu}$)
Silver ($\\text{Ag}$)
Gold ($\\text{Au}$)
e: Explanation: Option 0 selects zinc, which is an essential trace element in carbonic anhydrase, not cytochrome c oxidase. Option 1 is correct because **Copper ($\\text{Cu}$)** is an essential trace metal in cellular respiration. It serves as the core catalytic center in **Cytochrome C Oxidase** (the terminal electron-transfer protein complex, Complex IV, in the mitochondrial respiratory chain). The binuclear copper centers ($\\text{Cu}_A$ and $\\text{Cu}_B$) transfer electrons to reduce molecular oxygen into water, driving cellular ATP production. Option 2 and Option 3 select silver or gold, which have no respiratory enzyme functions.

qe:
Glauber's salt ($
\text{Na}_2
\text{SO}_4 \cdot 10
\text{H}_2
\text{O}$) and Epsom salt ($
\text{MgSO}_4 \cdot 7
\text{H}_2
\text{O}$) share a common medical application in pharmacology. What is their primary medical function when administered orally?
qh: ग्लाउबर लवण ($\\text{Na}_2\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) और एप्सम लवण ($\\text{MgSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$) औषध विज्ञान में एक सामान्य चिकित्सा अनुप्रयोग साझा करते हैं। मौखिक रूप से दिए जाने पर उनका प्राथमिक चिकित्सा कार्य क्या है?
o: They act as systemic anaesthetics that numb central pain receptors.
They act as saline purgatives (laxatives) that retain water in the intestinal lumen via osmotic pressure to relieve constipation.
They act as synthetic blood clotting agents that accelerate platelet aggregation.
They act as tooth enamel hardening agents.
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes central nervous system anaesthetics, which sulphate salts are not. Option 1 is correct because both **Glauber's Salt (Sodium Sulphate Decahydrate, $\\text{Na}_2\\text{SO}_4 \\cdot 10\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$)** and **Epsom Salt (Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate, $\\text{MgSO}_4 \\cdot 7\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$)** contain poorly absorbed divalent or sulphate ions. When administered orally in aqueous solutions, they remain in the intestinal tract and draw water into the bowel lumen via **Osmotic Pressure**, softening stool and stimulating peristalsis. Thus, both function medically as **Saline Purgatives / Laxatives**. Option 2 and Option 3 list blood clotting or enamel hardening roles.

qe: Mercury ($\\text{Hg}$, $Z=80$) forms alloys with almost all metals, termed amalgams. However, two specific metals resist amalgam formation, allowing mercury to be safely transported in containers made of one of them. Which pair of metals fails to form amalgams with mercury?
qh: पारा ($\\text{Hg}$, $Z=80$) लगभग सभी धातुओं के साथ मिश्र धातु बनाता है, जिन्हें अमलगम कहा जाता है। हालाँकि, दो विशिष्ट धातुएँ अमलगम बनने का विरोध करती हैं, जिससे पारे को उनमें से एक से बने कंटेनरों में सुरक्षित रूप से ले जाया जा सकता है। धातुओं का कौन सा जोड़ा पारे के साथ अमलगम बनाने में विफल रहता है?
o: Copper ($\\text{Cu}$) and Zinc ($\\text{Zn}$)
Iron ($\\text{Fe}$) and Platinum ($\\text{Pt}$)
Gold ($\\text{Au}$) and Silver ($\\text{Ag}$)
Sodium ($\\text{Na}$) and Lead ($\\text{Pb}$)
e: Explanation: Option 0 is incorrect because copper and zinc readily dissolve in mercury to form brass or zinc amalgams. Option 1 is correct because Iron ($\\text{Fe}$) and Platinum ($\\text{Pt}$) are classic exceptions that do not form **Amalgams** [alloys formed by mercury with other metals via metallic bonding and solvation]. The high cohesive energy and strong intermetallic lattice bonding of iron and platinum prevent mercury atoms from penetrating their metallic crystal lattice at ambient temperatures. Consequently, elemental mercury is transported and stored in **Iron Containers**. Option 2 is incorrect because gold and silver form amalgams very easily (a property exploited in cyanide/amalgamation gold extraction). Option 3 lists sodium and lead, both of which form reactive amalgams.

qe: When liquid mercury is exposed to atmospheric ozone gas ($\\text{O}_3$), it undergoes a physical change known as the 'tailing of mercury'. What surface phenomenon and chemical shift cause mercury to lose its characteristic meniscus and stick to glass walls?
qh: जब तरल पारे को वायुमंडलीय ओजोन गैस ($\\text{O}_3$) में रखा जाता है, तो यह एक भौतिक परिवर्तन से गुजरता है जिसे 'पारे का पुच्छन' (tailing of mercury) कहा जाता है। कौन सी सतह घटना और रासायनिक परिवर्तन पारे के अपने विशिष्ट मेनिसकस को खोने और कांच की दीवारों से चिपकने का कारण बनते हैं?
o: Reduction to elemental mercury gas, increasing surface tension.
Superficial oxidation to mercurous oxide ($\\text{Hg}_2\\text{O}$), which reduces surface tension and causes the liquid to wet glass.
Formation of mercuric chloride ($\\text{HgCl}_2$), which dissolves the glass surface.
Sublimation into ozone gas, producing a vacuum film.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly claims the metal is reduced and that surface tension increases. Option 1 is correct because ozone ($\\text{O}_3$) is a powerful oxidizing agent that reacts with the surface layer of mercury, causing **Superficial Oxidation** to form **Mercurous Oxide ($\\text{Hg}_2\\text{O}$)**: $2\\text{Hg} + \\text{O}_3 \\rightarrow \\text{Hg}_2\\text{O} + \\text{O}_2$. This sub-oxide film disrupts the extraordinarily high **Surface Tension** [the cohesive force per unit length acting along the surface of a liquid that minimizes its surface area] of pure mercury. As a result, the convex meniscus vanishes, and the oxidized liquid adheres to or 'wets' the glass container walls ('tailing'). Tailing can be reversed by shaking with dilute acid. Option 2 and Option 3 describe impossible chloride or vacuum sublimation paths.

qe: In qualitative inorganic analysis, Nessler's reagent is used as a sensitive laboratory test to detect ammonium ions ($\\text{NH}_4^+$) or dissolved ammonia gas. What is the active chemical complex present in Nessler's reagent, and from which mercury compound is it prepared?
qh: गुणात्मक अकार्बनिक विश्लेषण में, नेस्लर अभिकर्मक (Nessler's reagent) का उपयोग अमोनियम आयनों ($\\text{NH}_4^+$) या घुली हुई अमोनिया गैस का पता लगाने के लिए एक संवेदनशील प्रयोगशाला परीक्षण के रूप में किया जाता है। नेस्लर अभिकर्मक में मौजूद सक्रिय रासायनिक कॉम्प्लेक्स क्या है, और इसे किस पारे के यौगिक से तैयार किया जाता है?
o: $\\text{HgS}$ (Cinnabar) dissolved in nitric acid.
Potassium tetraiodomercurate(II) [$\\text{K}_2\\text{HgI}_4$] dissolved in an alkaline solution of $\\text{NaOH}$; prepared from Mercuric Chloride ($\\text{HgCl}_2$).
Mercurous chloride [$\\text{Hg}_2\\text{Cl}_2$, Calomel] mixed with alcohol.
Sodium argentocyanide [$\\text{Na}[\\text{Ag}(\\text{CN})_2]$] mixed with hydrogen peroxide.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies cinnabar as the reagent precursor. Option 1 is correct because **Nessler's Reagent** consists of an alkaline solution of **Potassium Tetraiodomercurate(II) [$\\text{K}_2\\text{HgI}_4$]** mixed with Sodium Hydroxide ($\\text{NaOH}$). It is synthesized by treating **Mercuric Chloride ($\\text{HgCl}_2$, corrosive sublimate)** with potassium iodide ($\\text{KI}$) until the initial red precipitate of $\\text{HgI}_2$ redissolves into the coordination complex. When added to a solution containing $\\text{NH}_4^+$ or $\\text{NH}_3$, it forms a characteristic brown precipitate or yellow-brown coloration of Iodide of Millon's base. Option 2 describes calomel (which is insoluble $\\text{Hg}_2\\text{Cl}_2$), and Option 3 lists a silver cyanocomplex.

qe: Mercuric Chloride ($\\text{HgCl}_2$), also known as corrosive sublimate, is a highly toxic, crystalline compound. In emergency toxicology, what common biological substance serves as the most effective immediate antidote for ingested corrosive sublimate?
qh: मर्क्यूरिक क्लोराइड ($\\text{HgCl}_2$), जिसे संक्षारक सब्लिमेट (corrosive sublimate) के रूप में भी जाना जाता है, एक अत्यधिक जहरीला, क्रिस्टलीय यौगic है। आपातकालीन विष विज्ञान में, कौन सा सामान्य जैविक पदार्थ निगले गए संक्षारक सब्लिमेट के लिए सबसे प्रभावी तत्काल विषनाशक (antidote) के रूप में कार्य करता है?
o: Vinegar (dilute acetic acid)
White of an egg (albumen)
Activated charcoal in concentrated alcohol
Sodium bicarbonate solution
e: Explanation: Option 0 is incorrect because acetic acid does not precipitate mercury ions effectively. Option 1 is correct because **Mercuric Chloride ($\\text{HgCl}_2$)** is an extremely toxic heavy metal salt that denatures cellular proteins and causes acute renal failure upon ingestion. The **White of an Egg (Egg Albumen)** contains dense soluble proteins (ovalbumin) rich in thiol and carboxyl functional groups. Upon ingestion, these proteins undergo **Protein Denaturation** [a structural alteration of proteins where heavy metal cations bind to functional groups, forming insoluble protein-metal precipitates]. The heavy mercury ions bind to the egg white proteins in the stomach, precipitating an insoluble mercury-albuminate complex before the toxin can be absorbed across the gastrointestinal tract. Option 2 and Option 3 do not bind heavy mercuric ions rapidly enough.

qe: Lead ($\\text{Pb}$, $Z=82$) undergoes oxidation in air and reacts with acids or alkalis. Why has the historical practice of using lead pipes for municipal drinking water distribution been globally banned?
qh: सीसा ($\\text{Pb}$, $Z=82$) हवा में ऑक्सीकरण से गुजरता है और अम्लों या क्षारों के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करता है। नगरपालिका के पेयजल वितरण के लिए सीसे के पाइपों का उपयोग करने की ऐतिहासिक प्रथा को विश्व स्तर पर क्यों प्रतिबंधित कर दिया गया है?
o: Lead pipes dissolve rapidly into gaseous chlorine, causing pipe implosions.
Lead reacts with dissolved oxygen and soft water to form soluble, highly toxic lead hydroxide [$\\text{Pb(OH)}_2$], leading to chronic plumbism.
Lead reacts with water to form explosive hydrogen gas in household taps.
Lead pipes solidify water into ice at room temperature.
e: Explanation: Option 0 introduces impossible gaseous chlorine dissolution. Option 1 is correct because soft water containing dissolved oxygen undergoes **Plumbosolvency** [the chemical property of water to dissolve lead from pipes]. Lead reacts with moist air and soft water to form soluble **Lead Hydroxide [$\\text{Pb(OH)}_2$]**: $2\\text{Pb} + \\text{O}_2 + 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O} \\rightarrow 2\\text{Pb(OH)}_2$. Ingesting this water delivers cumulative lead ions into the human body, causing severe neurological damage, renal toxicity, and anemia, collectively termed **Plumbism (Lead Poisoning)**. Hard water containing carbonates is slightly less dangerous because it forms an insoluble protective coating of $\\text{PbCO}_3$, but the use of lead piping remains banned due to health risks. Option 2 and Option 3 describe explosive gas evolution or phase changes.

qe: Lead forms multiple oxygen compounds with distinct chemical properties. What is the chemical formula of Red Lead (Minium or Sindhoor), and what structural oxide combination does it represent?
qh: सीसा अलग-अलग रासायनिक गुणों के साथ कई ऑक्सीजन यौगिक बनाता है। रेड लेड (मिनियम या सिंदूर) का रासायनिक सूत्र क्या है, और यह किस संरचनात्मक ऑक्साइड संयोजन का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है?
o: $\\text{PbO}$; simple monoxide (Litharge)
$\\text{Pb}_3\\text{O}_4$; mixed oxide representing $2\\text{PbO} \\cdot \\text{PbO}_2$ (Triplumbic Tetraoxide)
$\\text{PbO}_2$; simple dioxide (Lead peroxide)
$\\text{Pb(CH}_3\\text{COO)}_2$; organometallic acetate salt
e: Explanation: Option 0 describes Litharge ($\\text{PbO}$), a yellow simple oxide. Option 1 is correct because **Red Lead** (Minium or Sindhoor) is chemically **Triplumbic Tetraoxide ($\\text{Pb}_3\\text{O}_4$)**. It is classified as a **Mixed Oxide** [a stoichiometric compound containing an element in two distinct oxidation states within the same crystal lattice]. Structurally, it consists of two units of Lead(II) oxide and one unit of Lead(IV) oxide: **$2\\text{PbO} \\cdot \\text{PbO}_2$**, where lead exists simultaneously in the $+2$ and $+4$ oxidation states. It is prepared by heating litharge ($\\text{PbO}$) in air at $470^\\circ\\text{C}$ and is used as a red pigment in anti-rust primers. Option 2 is lead dioxide, and Option 3 is lead acetate (sugar of lead).

qe: Lead Acetate [$\\text{Pb(CH}_3\\text{COO)}_2$] is a water-soluble lead salt with a unique physical taste property. What is its common historical name, and what qualitative chemical test relies on it?
qh: लेड एसीटेट [$\\text{Pb(CH}_3\\text{COO)}_2$] एक पानी में घुलनशील सीसा लवण है जिसमें एक अद्वितीय भौतिक स्वाद गुण है। इसका सामान्य ऐतिहासिक नाम क्या है, और कौन सा गुणात्मक रासायनिक परीक्षण इस पर निर्भर करता है?
o: White Vitriol; used to test for ozone gas.
Sugar of Lead (Inorganic Sugar); used on filter paper to detect Hydrogen Sulfide gas ($\\text{H}_2\\text{S}$) by forming a black spot.
Lunar Caustic; used to detect ammonia gas.
Corrosive Sublimate; used to detect oxygen gas.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies lead acetate as White Vitriol (zinc sulphate). Option 1 is correct because **Lead Acetate [$\\text{Pb(CH}_3\\text{COO)}_2$]** forms sweet-tasting white crystals, earning it the historical name **Sugar of Lead** (or inorganic sugar), though it is toxic. In qualitative analytical chemistry, filter paper moistened with aqueous lead acetate is used as a diagnostic test for **Hydrogen Sulfide Gas ($\\text{H}_2\\text{S}$)**. When $\\text{H}_2\\text{S}$ contacts the paper, it reacts to form an insoluble, silvery-black spot of **Lead Sulfide ($\\text{PbS}$)**: $\\text{Pb(CH}_3\\text{COO)}_2 + \\text{H}_2\\text{S} \\rightarrow \\text{PbS}\\downarrow + 2\\text{CH}_3\\text{COOH}$. Option 2 and Option 3 list silver nitrate or mercuric chloride.

qe: Tetraethyl Lead [$\\text{Pb(C}_2\\text{H}_5)_4$, TEL] was added to commercial motor fuels for decades. What specific engine phenomenon did TEL suppress, and why was petrol containing TEL dyed red?
qh: टेट्राएथिल लेड [$\\text{Pb(C}_2\\text{H}_5)_4$, TEL] दशकों तक वाणिज्यिक मोटर ईंधनों में जोड़ा गया था। TEL ने किस विशिष्ट इंजन घटना को दबाया, और TEL युक्त पेट्रोल का रंग लाल क्यों रंगा गया था?
o: Suppressed fuel freezing; dyed red to increase thermal conductivity.
Suppressed premature fuel detonation ('knocking'); dyed red as a safety warning to indicate toxic leaded petrol ('ethyl petrol').
Suppressed carbon monoxide emission; dyed red to indicate high alcohol concentration.
Suppressed fuel evaporation; dyed red to enable magnetic attraction.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies TEL as an anti-freezing agent. Option 1 is correct because **Tetraethyl Lead [$\\text{Pb(C}_2\\text{H}_5)_4$]** acts as an **Anti-Knocking Agent** [a fuel additive that increases the octane rating of gasoline, preventing premature auto-ignition and shockwave rattling in internal combustion engine cylinders]. During combustion, TEL breaks down to form lead oxide particles that scavenge free radicals, smoothing the flame propagation front. Because organolead compounds are neurotoxic, petrol blended with TEL was dyed red to warn consumers of its toxicity, commercially marketed as 'ethyl petrol' or 'leaded petrol'. Option 2 and Option 3 describe unrelated emissions or evaporation features.

qe: Uranium ($Z=92$, $A=238$) is an actinide element with multiple naturally occurring isotopes. Which isotope of uranium is directly fissionable in thermal nuclear reactors, and what is its natural abundance percentage in mined uranium ore?
qh: यूरेनियम ($Z=92$, $A=238$) कई स्वाभाविक रूप से पाए जाने वाले आइसोटोप के साथ एक एक्टिनाइड तत्व है। यूरेनियम का कौन सा आइसोटोप थर्मल परमाणु रिएक्टरों में सीधे विखंडनीय (fissionable) है, और खनन किए गए यूरेनियम अयस्क में इसकी प्राकृतिक प्रचुरता प्रतिशत क्या है?
o: $\\text{U}-235$; abundance: $0.71\\%$
$\\text{U}-234$; abundance: $50.0\\%$
$\\text{U}-232$; abundance: $12.5\\%$
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists $\\text{U}-238$, which is the most abundant isotope ($99.28\\%$) but is fertile rather than directly fissionable by thermal neutrons. Option 1 is correct because natural uranium extracted from pitchblende contains three primary radioactive isotopes: $\\text{U}-238$ ($99.28\\%$), $\\text{U}-235$ ($0.71\\%$), and $\\text{U}-234$ ($0.006\\%$). **Uranium-235 ($\\text{U}-235$)** is the only naturally occurring **Fissile Isotope** [a nuclide capable of undergoing nuclear fission upon absorbing low-energy thermal neutrons, sustaining a nuclear chain reaction]. Because its natural concentration is only **$0.71\%$**, nuclear fuels often require isotopic enrichment to operate effectively in light-water reactors. Option 2 and Option 3 list incorrect abundance figures.

qe: Thorium ($Z=90$, $A=232$) is a naturally occurring actinide metal found abundantly in coastal mineral sands. What mineral ore serves as the chief source of Thorium, and in which Indian coastal state are these reserves prominently concentrated?
qh: थोरियम ($Z=90$, $A=232$) तटीय खनिज रेत में बहुतायत से पाया जाने वाला एक प्राकृतिक एक्टिनाइड धातु है। कौन सा खनिज अयस्क थोरियम के मुख्य स्रोत के रूप में कार्य करता है, और भारत के किस तटीय राज्य में ये भंडार प्रमुख रूप से केंद्रित हैं?
o: Pitchblende ore; concentrated in Rajasthan.
Monazite sand; concentrated in the coastal beach sands of Kerala.
Cassiterite ore; concentrated in Gujarat.
Bauxite ore; concentrated in Bihar.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies pitchblende (which is the principal ore of uranium). Option 1 is correct because **Thorium ($\\text{Th}$)** is an $f$-block actinide metal extracted primarily from **Monazite Sand** [a reddish-brown phosphate mineral sand containing rare-earth metals and up to $8-10\\%$ thorium oxide]. India possesses some of the world's largest reserves of monazite, densely concentrated along the beach sands of **Kerala** (and parts of Tamil Nadu and Odisha). Thorium is a fertile nuclear fuel that can be converted into fissile $\\text{U}-233$ in breeder reactors. Option 2 lists tin ore, and Option 3 lists aluminium ore.

qe: Mineral ore beneficiation involves separating gangue from valuable metal minerals. What physical property difference forms the basis of Hydraulic Washing (Gravity Separation), and for which ores is it applied?
qh: खनिज अयस्क सज्जीकरण (Ore beneficiation) में मूल्यवान धातु खनिजों से गैंग (gangue) को अलग करना शामिल है। भौतिक गुणों का कौन सा अंतर हाइड्रोलिक वाशिंग (गुरुत्वाकर्षण पृथक्करण) का आधार बनता है, और यह किन अयस्कों के लिए लागू होता है?
o: Difference in magnetic susceptibility; applied to sulphide ores.
Difference in specific gravities (densities) between heavy ore particles and lighter gangue particles; applied to iron oxides ($\\text{Fe}_2\\text{O}_3, \\text{Fe}_3\\text{O}_4$) and native gold.
Difference in solubility in sodium cyanide; applied to bauxite.
Difference in boiling points; applied to liquid mercury.
e: Explanation: Option 0 confuses gravity separation with magnetic separation. Option 1 is correct because **Hydraulic Washing** is a **Gravity Separation** technique based on the difference in **Specific Gravities (Densities)** of the dense ore particles versus the lighter gangue (earthy impurities). Powdered ore is passed over a sloped, grooved table in a running stream of water; the buoyant, lighter gangue particles are washed away, while the heavier ore particles (such as iron oxides $\\text{Fe}_2\\text{O}_3, \\text{Fe}_3\\text{O}_4$, tin stone $\\text{SnO}_2$, or native gold) settle into the grooves. Option 2 describes chemical leaching, and Option 3 describes distillation.

qe: Froth Floatation is an industrial ore concentration process. What specific class of mineral ores is concentrated using Froth Floatation, and what roles do pine oil and cresols play?
qh: झाग प्लवन (Froth Floatation) एक औद्योगिक अयस्क सांद्रण प्रक्रिया है। झाग प्लवन का उपयोग करके किस विशिष्ट वर्ग के खनिज अयस्कों को सांद्रित किया जाता है, और चीड़ का तेल (pine oil) तथा क्रेसोल (cresols) क्या भूमिका निभाते हैं?
o: Carbonate ores; pine oil acts as a solvent, cresols act as acidic fluxes.
Sulphide ores ($\\text{PbS}, \\text{ZnS}, \\text{CuFeS}_2$); pine oil acts as a collector to wet ore particles, cresols act as froth stabilizers.
Oxide ores; pine oil acts as a magnetic core, cresols act as reducing agents.
Halide ores; pine oil acts as an oxidizing agent, cresols act as anti-foaming agents.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly applies froth floatation to carbonate ores. Option 1 is correct because **Froth Floatation** relies on differential surface wettability and is used specifically for **Sulphide Ores** (e.g., galena $\\text{PbS}$, zinc blende $\\text{ZnS}$, copper pyrites $\\text{CuFeS}_2$). Powdered ore is suspended in water containing additives: **Pine Oil** acts as a **Collector** [a surfactant that selectively wets sulphide ore particles, making them hydrophobic], while **Cresols / Aniline** act as **Froth Stabilizers** [compounds that stabilize air bubbles so the mineral-laden froth can be skimmed off]. Earthy gangue particles are wetted by water and sink to the bottom. Option 2 and Option 3 describe incorrect ore classes or additive functions.

qe: Leaching is a chemical concentration method where an ore selectively dissolves in a reagent while gangue remains insoluble. Which reagents are used for the chemical leaching of Bauxite ore and Gold/Silver ores respectively?
qh: लीचिंग (Leaching) एक रासायनिक सांद्रण विधि है जहाँ एक अयस्क चुनिंदा रूप से एक अभिकर्मक में घुल जाता है जबकि गैंग अघुलनशील रहता है। बॉक्साइट अयस्क और सोना/चांदी अयस्कों के रासायनिक लीचिंग के लिए क्रमशः किन अभिकर्मकों का उपयोग किया जाता है?
o: Bauxite: Concentrated $\\text{HCl}$; Gold/Silver: Concentrated $\\text{H}_2\\text{SO}_4$
Bauxite: Concentrated $\\text{NaOH}$ solution; Gold/Silver: Dilute solution of Sodium Cyanide ($\\text{NaCN}$) or Potassium Cyanide ($\\text{KCN}$) in the presence of air.
Bauxite: Liquid ammonia; Gold/Silver: Molten sodium carbonate.
Bauxite: Distilled water; Gold/Silver: Kerosene oil.
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists mineral acids that do not selectively leach alumina or form cyanide complexes. Option 1 is correct because **Chemical Leaching** relies on selective solubility: (1) **Bauxite Ore ($\\text{Al}_2\\text{O}_3 \\cdot 2\\text{H}_2\\text{O}$)** is leached with concentrated **$\\text{NaOH}$ Solution** at $140-150^\\circ\\text{C}$ (Baeyer's Process), dissolving amphoteric alumina as soluble sodium aluminate [$\\text{NaAl(OH)}_4$] while leaving iron oxide gangue insoluble; (2) **Gold and Silver** are leached with a dilute solution of **$\\text{NaCN}$ or $\\text{KCN}$** in the presence of atmospheric oxygen, forming soluble cyano-complexes [$\\text{Na}[\\text{Au}(\\text{CN})_2]$ or $\\text{Na}[\\text{Ag}(\\text{CN})_2]$]. Option 2 and Option 3 list non-selective solvents.

qe: Converting concentrated ores into metal oxides is a prerequisite for chemical reduction. What metallurgical distinction separates Calcination from Roasting?
qh: सांद्रित अयस्कों को धातु ऑक्साइड में बदलना रासायनिक अपचयन के लिए एक पूर्व शर्त है। कौन सा धातुकर्म अंतर निस्तापन (Calcination) को भर्जन (Roasting) से अलग करता है?
o: Calcination heats sulphide ores in excess air; Roasting heats carbonate ores in a vacuum.

Calcination heats carbonate, hydroxide, or oxide ores below their melting point in the absence or limited supply of air; Roasting heats sulphide ores below their melting point in a continuous, regular supply of air.
Calcination operates above $3000^\\circ\\text{C}$; Roasting operates at absolute zero.
Calcination converts metals into amalgams; Roasting dissolves metals in cyanide.
e: Explanation: Option 0 reverses the ore types and air conditions for calcination versus roasting. Option 1 is correct because: (1) **Calcination** involves heating carbonate ($\\text{CaCO}_3, \\text{MgCO}_3$), hydroxide ($\\text{Al(OH)}_3$), or hydrated oxide ores in the **absence or limited supply of air** below their melting point to drive off volatile moisture and $\\text{CO}_2$, leaving a porous metal oxide; (2) **Roasting** involves heating **Sulphide Ores** ($\\text{PbS}, \\text{ZnS}, \\text{CuFeS}_2$) in a **continuous, regular supply of air** below their melting point to oxidize sulfur and arsenic into volatile gases ($\\text{SO}_2, \\text{As}_2\\text{O}_3$), converting the metal into an oxide. Option 2 and Option 3 present invalid thermal or solvent claims.

qe: During smelting, a chemical additive called a 'flux' is introduced into the furnace. What is the fundamental chemical purpose of a flux, and what compound forms when it reacts with gangue?
qh: प्रगलन (Smelting) के दौरान, एक रासायनिक योजक जिसे 'फ्लक्स' (flux) कहा जाता है, भट्टी में पेश किया जाता है। फ्लक्स का मौलिक रासायनिक उद्देश्य क्या है, और जब यह गैंग के साथ प्रतिक्रिया करता है तो कौन सा यौगिक बनता है?
o: To oxidize the metal into gas; forms volatile nitric oxide.
To react with infusible gangue (impurities) present in the ore to convert it into a fusible, low-density waste material called 'Slag'.
To lower the electrical conductivity of the furnace; forms solid lead amalgam.
To convert liquid iron into radioactive uranium.
e: Explanation: Option 0 misidentifies flux as a gas-producing oxidant. Option 1 is correct because high-temperature **Smelting** requires removing non-fusible earthy impurities (gangue) remaining in roasted/calcined ores. A **Flux** is a chemical reagent added to react with these infusible impurities: an **Acidic Flux** (such as Silica, $\\text{SiO}_2$) is added to remove basic impurities ($\\text{FeO}, \\text{CaO}$), while a **Basic Flux** (such as Lime, $\\text{CaO}$, or Limestone, $\\text{CaCO}_3$) is added to remove acidic impurities ($\\text{SiO}_2$). The chemical reaction between flux and gangue yields a fusible, light, molten silicate layer called **Slag**: $\\text{Flux} + \\text{Impurity} \\rightarrow \\text{Slag}$. Slag floats on top of molten metal and is tapped off. Option 2 and Option 3 describe amalgam or transmutation claims.

qe:
In the blast furnace extraction of iron from haematite ($
\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$), limestone ($
\text{CaCO}_3$) is added along with coke and ore. What specific chemical role does limestone perform during this smelting operation?
qh: हेमेटाइट ($\\text{Fe}_2\\text{O}_3$) से लोहे के ब्लास्ट फर्नेस निष्कर्षण में, कोक और अयस्क के साथ चूना पत्थर ($\\text{CaCO}_3$) मिलाया जाता है। इस प्रगलन कार्य के दौरान चूना पत्थर कौन सी विशिष्ट रासायनिक भूमिका निभाता है?
o: Acts as a reducing agent that converts iron oxide directly into pig iron.
Decomposes to form Calcium Oxide ($\\text{CaO}$), which serves as a basic flux that reacts with acidic silica gangue ($\\text{SiO}_2$) to form fusible calcium silicate slag ($\\text{CaSiO}_3$).
Acts as an anti-knocking agent that prevents furnace explosions.
Acts as a catalyst that converts nitrogen into ammonia gas.
e: Explanation: Option 0 confuses limestone with coke/carbon monoxide (the actual reducing agents). Option 1 is correct because haematite ore contains acidic **Silica ($\\text{SiO}_2$)** as its chief gangue impurity. **Limestone ($\\text{CaCO}_3$)** added to the blast furnace decomposes at high temperatures ($800-1000^\\circ\\text{C}$) into quicklime and carbon dioxide: $\\text{CaCO}_3 \\xrightarrow{\\Delta} \\text{CaO} + \\text{CO}_2\\uparrow$. **Calcium Oxide ($\\text{CaO}$)** acts as a **Basic Flux**, reacting with the acidic silica gangue to form molten **Calcium Silicate Slag ($\\text{CaSiO}_3$)**: $\\text{CaO} + \\text{SiO}_2 \\rightarrow \\text{CaSiO}_3$. Slag floats on the heavier molten iron, preventing re-oxidation. Option 2 and Option 3 list engine antiknock or Haber catalyst functions.

qe: Lead-based alloys are engineered for joining electrical circuits and casting printing type. What are the elemental compositions of Solder and Type Metal respectively?
qh: सीसा-आधारित मिश्र धातुओं (Lead-based alloys) को विद्युत सर्किट को जोड़ने और मुद्रण प्रकार (printing type) की ढलाई के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। क्रमशः सोल्डर (Solder) और टाइप मेटल (Type metal) की तात्विक संरचनाएँ क्या हैं?
o: Solder: Tin [$\\text{Sn}$\\ ($50\text{--}70\\%$)] and Lead [$\\text{Pb}$\\ ($50\text{--}30\\%$)][Eutectic Blend]; Type Metal: Lead [$\\text{Pb}$\\ ($75\\%$)]+ Antimony [$\\text{Sb}$\\ ($20\\%$)]+ Tin [$\\text{Sn}$\\ ($6\\%$)].
Solder: Pure gold ($100\\%$); Type Metal: Mercury ($90\\%$) + Lead ($10\\%$)
Solder: Aluminium ($95\\%$) + Copper ($5\\%$); Type Metal: Uranium ($100\\%$)
e: Explanation: Option 0 lists brass or steel compositions. Option 1 is correct because: (1) **Solder** is a low-melting fusible alloy composed of **Tin ($\\text{Sn}$, $50-70\\%$) and Lead ($\\text{Pb}$, $50-30\\%$)** used to join electrical components and copper wiring; (2) **Type Metal** is a specialized casting alloy composed of **Lead ($\\text{Pb}$, $75\\%$), Antimony ($\\text{Sb}$, $20\\%$), and Tin ($\\text{Sn}$, $6\\%$)**. Antimony is added because it expands upon cooling, allowing the molten alloy to completely fill detailed casting molds for sharp printing typefaces. Option 2 and Option 3 list gold, mercury, or radioactive uranium distractors.

qe:
Mercury ($
\text{Hg}$) displays unique electrical properties under thermal variation. At what cryogenic temperature threshold does liquid/solid mercury lose all electrical resistance to become a superconductor?
qh: पारा ($\\text{Hg}$) तापीय भिन्नता के तहत अद्वितीय विद्युत गुण प्रदर्शित करता है। किस क्रायोजेनिक तापमान सीमा पर तरल/ठोस पारा अतिचालक (superconductor) बनने के लिए सभी विद्युत प्रतिरोध खो देता है?
o: $4.12\\text{ K}$ (approx $-269^\\circ\\text{C}$)
$100\\text{ K}$ (approx $-173^\\circ\\text{C}$)
$0\\text{ K}$ (Absolute Zero exact)
e: Explanation: Option 0 is the freezing point of water ($0^\\circ\\text{C}$), where mercury is a normal liquid metal. Option 1 is correct because in 1911, Dutch physicist Heike Kamerlingh Onnes discovered **Superconductivity** [the state of zero electrical resistance and expulsion of interior magnetic flux fields occurring in certain materials below a characteristic critical temperature] using solid mercury. When cooled with liquid helium down to **$4.12\text{ K}$**, mercury's electrical resistivity drops abruptly to zero, allowing electric currents to flow indefinitely without thermal dissipation. Option 2 and Option 3 list higher non-critical temperatures.

qe:
Mercuric Sulphide ($
\text{HgS}$) occurs naturally as cinnabar ore and is used as a red pigment under the name vermillion. What reagent mixture is required to dissolve red mercuric sulphide?
qh: मर्क्यूरिक सल्फाइड ($\\text{HgS}$) स्वाभाविक रूप से सिनाबार अयस्क के रूप में होता है और इसका उपयोग वर्मिलियन (सिंदूर) नाम से लाल वर्णक के रूप में किया जाता है। लाल मर्क्यूरिक सल्फाइड को घोलने के लिए किस अभिकर्मक मिश्रण की आवश्यकता होती है?
o: Cold dilute hydrochloric acid alone
Aqua-regia (concentrated $\\text{HCl}$ and concentrated $\\text{HNO}_3$ in 3:1 ratio)
Aqueous sodium hydroxide solution
Distilled water saturated with carbon dioxide
e: Explanation: Option 0 is incorrect because $\\text{HgS}$ has an extremely low solubility product ($K_{sp} \\approx 10^{-52}$) and resists single mineral acids. Option 1 is correct because **Mercuric Sulphide ($\\text{HgS}$, Vermillion)** is insoluble in water, dilute alkalis, and single concentrated mineral acids ($\\text{HCl}, \\text{HNO}_3, \\text{H}_2\\text{SO}_4$). It dissolves only in **Aqua-Regia** [a 3:1 mixture of concentrated $\\text{HCl}$ and concentrated $\\text{HNO}_3$], where nitric acid oxidizes sulphide ions to free sulfur or sulphate, while hydrochloric acid provides chloride ions to form the stable soluble complex $\\text{HgCl}_4^{2-}$ (or mercuric chloride, $\\text{HgCl}_2$). Option 2 and Option 3 list alkalis or carbonated water, which cannot dissolve $\\text{HgS}$.

qe: Heavy transition metals exhibit distinct physical transport and electrical properties. Which choice correctly pairs the metal that exhibits high electrical resistance with its key physical transport feature?
qh: भारी संक्रमण धातुएं विशिष्ट भौतिक परिवहन और विद्युत गुण प्रदर्शित करती हैं। कौन सा विकल्प उस धातु को उसकी प्रमुख भौतिक परिवहन विशेषता के साथ सही ढंग से मिलाता है जो उच्च विद्युत प्रतिरोध प्रदर्शित करती है?
o: Lead: Liquid at room temperature, transported in copper tubes.
Mercury ($\\text{Hg}$): Liquid transition metal with unusually high electrical resistance, transported in iron containers due to non-amalgamation.
Uranium: Highly ductile gas, transported in wooden crates.
Thorium: Superconductor at room temperature, transported in glass jars.
e: Explanation: Option 0 incorrectly identifies lead as a liquid at room temperature. Option 1 is correct because **Mercury ($\\text{Hg}$)** is a liquid transition metal with an unusually low electrical conductivity (high electrical resistance) compared to other metals like copper or silver. Because it forms amalgams with most metals but fails to react with or amalgamate iron, elemental mercury is stored and transported industrially in **Iron Containers**. Option 2 incorrectly calls uranium a ductile gas, and Option 3 incorrectly describes thorium as a room-temperature superconductor.
